# WebKit CSS port ledger

- **Upstream:** `C:\Users\dylan\repos\WebKit` @ `300e80c70fd3` (2025-12-26). Never update the clone mid-port.
- **Paths** are relative to `Source/WebCore` (WebKit) and `Krystal.Booey/include/Krystal.Booey` (Krystal) unless stated.
- **Regenerate a slice:** `python tools/graph.py <entries...> --headers-only --out build/port/<slice>.md`, from the repository root (the output is temporary and untracked; the `tools/port/out/` paths in older sections were committed under `Krystal.Booey/` once and have been deleted, so regenerate them if needed. To traverse outside `css/` and `style/`, pass all prefixes: `--follow css/ style/ platform/graphics/`; `--follow` replaces the defaults)

## Verdicts

| Verdict | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `?` | Undecided. |
| `have?` | Krystal file matched by name only, needs confirming. `have*?` = matched and looks simplified. |
| `have` | Already ported; matches upstream closely enough to diff against. |
| `have*` | Already exists, but simplified/restructured or written from the spec; don't expect a line-by-line match. |
| `port` | Will port. |
| `stub` | Needed for compilation, but only a minimal stand-in. |
| `wont` | Not supported; remove the dependency at the include site. |

Status (for `port`/`have*`) is tracked in Notes: `compiles`, `tested`.

## Resize observers (B5a, 2026-10-24)

Step B5a of observers (*B5 plan* in `docs/booey/ROADMAP.md`): `ResizeObserver`, made from C++ with a callback, reports the content and border box sizes of the elements it observes in the rendering update's resize observations step, round by round deeper into the tree, with layout between rounds; observations no deeper than the last round's are left for the next update and reported as an error at the window. The document's own observer keeps the last remembered sizes of `contain-intrinsic-size: auto` boxes, which a box whose contents are skipped uses. Graph from `page/ResizeObserver.h` (headers-only, following `page/`): 7 files, all ported here; its boundaries are ported (`Element`, `DOMRectReadOnly`, the geometry) or have no counterpart (the bindings, `ActiveDOMCallback`, `CallbackResult`, `GCReachableRef`, the inspector, the lock and logging), since `ResizeObserverCallback` is a `Func`, as `MutationCallback`.

|---|---|---|---|---|
| `page/ResizeObserver.h`, `.cpp` | `port*` | `Page/ResizeObserver.hpp`, `src/Page/ResizeObserver.cpp` (new) | on | tested. No lock, wrapper reachability or `callbackConcurrently` (no garbage collector); the targets waiting for their first observation and the active ones are held by `Ref`, where upstream holds them weakly and keeps them alive from the wrapper. |
| `page/ResizeObservation.h`, `.cpp` | `port*` | `Page/ResizeObservation.hpp`, `src/Page/ResizeObservation.cpp` (new) | on | tested. No SVG bounding boxes (FIXME) or frame owners (the depth counts the target's document only); no stream output. |

| `page/ResizeObserverCallback.h` | `port*` | `Page/ResizeObserverCallback.hpp` (new) | on | a `Func` taking the entries and the observer. |
| `dom/Document.h`, `.cpp` (`addResizeObserver`, `removeResizeObserver`, `hasResizeObservers`, `gatherResizeObservations`, `gatherResizeObservationsForContainIntrinsicSize`, `deliverResizeObservations`, `hasSkippedResizeObservations`, `setHasSkippedResizeObservations`, `updateResizeObservations`, `observeForContainIntrinsicSize`, `unobserveForContainIntrinsicSize`, `resetObservationSizeForContainIntrinsicSize`, `CallbackForContainIntrinsicSize`, the observers' half of `commonTeardown`) | `port*` | `dom::Document` | on | tested; `CommonTeardown` (new) only disconnects the observers, from `RemovedLastRef` and `WillBeRemovedFromFrame`. |

**Bugs fixed:**
- `Element.cpp` used `HTMLDialogElement` without including it, and compiled only because the unity build put it after a file that did.
**Added (upstream API):** `ResizeObserver`, `ResizeObservation`, `ResizeObserverEntry`, `ResizeObserverSize`, `ResizeObserverOptions`, `ResizeObserverBoxOptions`, `ResizeObserverCallback`, `ResizeObserverData`; `Document::AddResizeObserver`, `RemoveResizeObserver`, `HasResizeObservers`, `GatherResizeObservations`, `GatherResizeObservationsForContainIntrinsicSize`, `DeliverResizeObservations`, `HasSkippedResizeObservations`, `SetHasSkippedResizeObservations`, `ObserveForContainIntrinsicSize`, `UnobserveForContainIntrinsicSize`, `ResetObservationSizeForContainIntrinsicSize`; `Element::EnsureResizeObserverData`, `ResizeObserverDataIfExists`, `LastRememberedLogicalWidth`, `LastRememberedLogicalHeight`, `SetLastRememberedLogicalWidth`, `SetLastRememberedLogicalHeight`, `ClearLastRememberedLogicalWidth`, `ClearLastRememberedLogicalHeight`; `ScopeExit`, `MakeScopeExit`.
**Differences:**
- The callback is a C++ `Func`, not the specification's callback interface (no `this` value or exceptions to report); native observers use the same type, told apart by how they're made (`CreateNativeObserver`).
- `Document::UpdateResizeObservations` takes the page (as upstream), now that it lays out between rounds; the loop error is reported with `LocalDOMWindow::ReportError` (an `ErrorEvent`, then the console), as upstream's `reportException`.
- Whoever made an observer keeps it; it disconnects when destroyed, and the document's list holds it weakly, as upstream.
- No quirk silencing resize observers. The content visibility state's initial determination in the loop is B5d's (FIXME).
Tests: `tests/Page/ResizeObserver.cpp` (3 cases / 56 assertions: content and border boxes, the first observation, elements without boxes, writing modes and zoom, unobserving, disconnecting and destroying; deeper changes in the same update, shallower ones skipped with the loop error, removed and destroyed targets; the last remembered size used while the contents are skipped, forgotten without `auto` and after removal). `tests/Style/AnchorPositionEvaluator.cpp` passes the page to `UpdateResizeObservations`. The whole Booey suite passes (2694 cases; 7 expected failures), and so does Krystal.UI's (103).

## Intersection observers (B5b, 2026-10-24)

Step B5b of observers (*B5 plan* in `docs/booey/ROADMAP.md`): `IntersectionObserver`, made from C++ with a callback, reports how much of each element it observes intersects its root (an element, a document, or the main frame's viewport for an implicit root), grown by its root and scroll margins, whenever the ratio crosses one of its thresholds; the rendering update's intersection observations step updates and notifies the observers its document tracks, and a target's first observation comes in the next update once the document has loaded, or after two seconds while it's loading. Graph from `page/IntersectionObserver.h` (headers-only, following `css/`, `style/` and `page/`): 156 files, nearly all already ported or reached through the margin parser and the style values; new here are the four `page/IntersectionObserver*` files. Its boundaries are ported (`Element`, `DOMRectReadOnly`, the parser, the geometry, `VisibleRectContext`, `LocalFrameView`) or have no counterpart (the bindings, `ActiveDOMCallback`, `CallbackResult`, `GCReachableRef`, the inspector, logging, security origins and the frame tree), since `IntersectionObserverCallback` is a `Func`, as `ResizeObserverCallback`.

| WebKit | Verdict | Krystal | CMake | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `page/IntersectionObserver.h`, `.cpp` | `port*` | `Page/IntersectionObserver.hpp`, `src/Page/IntersectionObserver.cpp` (new) | on | tested. No frame tree: `computeClippedRectInRootContentsSpace` stops at the main frame, every observation is same-origin (the root margin applies and `rootBounds` is reported), and the intersection rect needs no mapping between frames. No pending targets or wrapper reachability (no garbage collector; the entries hold their targets); the targets waiting for their first observation are held by `Ref`. `takeRecords` returns the entries only. `IncludeObscuredInsets` is kept for B5d, but there are no obscured insets, so it's the layout viewport either way. |
| `page/IntersectionObserverEntry.h`, `.cpp` | `port` | `Page/IntersectionObserverEntry.hpp`, `src/Page/IntersectionObserverEntry.cpp` (new) | on | tested; no stream output. |
| `page/IntersectionObserverMarginBox.h` | `port` | `Page/IntersectionObserverMarginBox.hpp` (new) | on | tested. |
| `page/IntersectionObserverCallback.h` | `port*` | `Page/IntersectionObserverCallback.hpp` (new) | on | a `Func` taking the entries and the observer. |
| `dom/Document.h`, `.cpp` (`addIntersectionObserver`, `removeIntersectionObserver`, `numberOfIntersectionObservers`, `updateIntersectionObservations`, `scheduleInitialIntersectionObservationUpdate`, the initial update timer and `scheduleRenderingUpdate`'s part, `ensureIntersectionObserverData`, `intersectionObserverDataIfExists`, the observers' part of the destructor and `commonTeardown`) | `port*` | `dom::Document` | on | tested; no deferring by the page (`shouldDeferIntersectionObservations`, FIXME). |
| `dom/Element.h`, `.cpp`, `ElementRareData.h` (`ensureIntersectionObserverData`, `intersectionObserverDataIfExists`, `disconnectFromIntersectionObservers`, moving the observers in `didMoveToNewDocument`) | `port` | `dom::Element` (`OnAdopt`, new), `ElementRareData` | on | tested, except moving to another document. |
| `page/Page.h`, `.cpp` (`RenderingUpdateStep::IntersectionObservations` and its step) | `port` | `Page` | on | after focus fixup, as upstream. |
| `rendering/VisibleRectContext.h` (`scrollMargin`), `rendering/RenderBox.cpp` (the scroll margin in `applyCachedClipAndScrollPosition`) | `port` | `VisibleRectContext`, `RenderBox` | on | tested; the FIXMEs went. |
| `page/LocalFrameView.h`, `.cpp` (`baseLayoutViewportSize`, `layoutViewportRect`, `absoluteToClientRect`, `absoluteToLayoutViewportRect`) | `port*` | `LocalFrameView` | on | tested through the observers. No visual viewports, so the layout viewport is at the scroll position (FIXME). |
| `wtf/Vector.h` (`removeFirstMatching`) | `port*` | `Krystal.Core/Types/List.hpp` (`RemoveFirstMatching`) | on | shared by both observers, which each had a copy. |

**Bugs fixed:** none.
**Added (upstream API):** `IntersectionObserver` (`Init`, `Create`, `TrackingDocument`, `Root`, `RootMargin`, `ScrollMargin`, `RootMarginBox`, `ScrollMarginBox`, `Thresholds`, `ObservationTargets`, `HasObservationTargets`, `IsObserving`, `Observe`, `Unobserve`, `Disconnect`, `TakeRecords`, `TargetDestroyed`, `RootDestroyed`, `UpdateObservations`, `NowTimestamp`, `AppendQueuedEntry`, `Notify`), `IntersectionObserverEntry`, `IntersectionObserverMarginEdge`, `IntersectionObserverMarginBox`, `IntersectionObserverCallback`, `IntersectionObserverData`, `IntersectionObserverRegistration`, `IncludeObscuredInsets`; `Document::AddIntersectionObserver`, `RemoveIntersectionObserver`, `NumberOfIntersectionObservers`, `UpdateIntersectionObservations`, `ScheduleInitialIntersectionObservationUpdate`, `EnsureIntersectionObserverData`, `IntersectionObserverDataIfExists`; `Element::EnsureIntersectionObserverData`, `IntersectionObserverDataIfExists`, `OnAdopt`; `VisibleRectContext::ScrollMargin`; `LocalFrameView::BaseLayoutViewportSize`, `LayoutViewportRect`, `AbsoluteToClientRect`, `AbsoluteToLayoutViewportRect`; `RenderingUpdateStep::IntersectionObservations`; `RemoveFirstMatching`.
**Differences:**
- The callback is a C++ `Func`, not the specification's callback interface (as resize observers); the document that made the observer stands in for the callback's context, for the timestamp.
- Observers are notified in the rendering update, as upstream, where the specification queues a task.
- Whoever made an observer keeps it; it disconnects when destroyed, and its root's and its targets' data hold it weakly, as upstream.
Tests: `tests/Page/IntersectionObserver.cpp` (4 cases / 160 assertions: the defaults, parsing margins and their errors, sorting and checking thresholds, roots; the implicit root's first observations and changes on scrolling, thresholds, root margins in pixels and percentages, taking records before delivery, unobserving and disconnecting; an element root's scrolled contents, the implicit root through a scroller's clip with and without a scroll margin, a target outside its root; removed and destroyed targets, a destroyed root, a destroyed observer). The whole Booey suite passes (2698 cases; 7 expected failures), and so does Krystal.UI's (103).

## Lazy images (B5c, 2026-10-24)

Step B5c of observers (*B5 plan* in `docs/booey/ROADMAP.md`): an `<img loading=lazy>` defers its fetch until it intersects the viewport, or comes within a scrollport of a scroll container's clip (the scroll margin is `100%`), as one intersection observer per document (`LazyLoadImageObserver`) reports; deferred images paint nothing, and changing `loading` away from `lazy` loads at once. Graph from `html/LazyLoadImageObserver.h` (headers-only, following `css/`, `style/`, `page/` and `html/`): 51 files, all ported (the intersection observer and its boundaries, B5b) except `html/LazyLoadImageObserver` itself. `CachedResourceLoader` already deferred loads (`ImageLoading::DeferredUntilVisible`, G7b), so only the image loader's side was missing.

| WebKit | Verdict | Krystal | CMake | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `html/LazyLoadImageObserver.h`, `.cpp` | `port*` | `HTML/LazyLoadImageObserver.hpp`, `src/HTML/LazyLoadImageObserver.cpp` (new) | on | tested. The callback is a function rather than a callback class (`IntersectionObserverCallback` is a `Func`). |
| `loader/ImageLoader.h`, `.cpp` (`LazyImageLoadState`, `loadDeferredImage`, `isDeferred`, `resetLazyImageLoading`, `canReuseFromListOfAvailableImages`, and their parts in `updateFromElement`, `didUpdateCachedImage`, `notifyFinished` and `elementDidMoveToNewDocument`) | `port*` | `ImageLoader` | on | tested, except moving to another document. `canReuseFromListOfAvailableImages` has no sessions, preloads or origins (FIXMEs); no `lazyImageLoadingEnabled` setting (a standard feature, always on). |
| `html/HTMLImageElement.h`, `.cpp` (`loadDeferredImage`, `isDeferred`, `isLazyLoadable`, `hasLazyLoadableAttributeValue`, `loading` in `attributeChanged`; `loading` reflected with its known values) | `port*` | `html::HTMLImageElement` | on | tested. Scripting is the host's flag (`MediaEnvironment::CanExecuteScripts`, as the `scripting` media feature) in place of the frame's script controller: without it, or without a frame, images load eagerly, as upstream. `loading`'s keywords are an `EnumeratedAttribute` (`AttributeState::Lazy`, `Eager`, new). |
| `dom/Document.h`, `.cpp` (`lazyLoadImageObserver`) | `port` | `dom::Document` (`GetLazyLoadImageObserver`) | on | tested. |
| `rendering/RenderImage.cpp` (`isDeferredImage` in `paintReplaced`) | `port` | `RenderImage` | on | tested; the FIXME went. |

**Bugs fixed:** none.
**Added (upstream API):** `html::LazyLoadImageObserver` (`Observe`, `Unobserve`, `IsObserved`); `LazyImageLoadState`, `ImageLoader::LoadDeferredImage`, `IsDeferred`; `HTMLImageElement::LoadDeferredImage`, `IsDeferred`, `IsLazyLoadable`, `HasLazyLoadableAttributeValue`; `Document::GetLazyLoadImageObserver`; `AttributeState::Lazy`, `Eager`.
**Differences:**
- As upstream, the observer's root margin is zero and only scroll containers' clips grow (by `100%`), so an image in the document's own scrolling loads once it's in the viewport.
- `LocalFrameView::ViewportContentsChanged`'s FIXME no longer lists intersection observers and lazy loading (neither is upstream's there); the visible viewport rect is left.
Tests: `tests/HTML/LazyLoadImageObserver.cpp` (4 cases / 47 assertions: `loading`'s known values; images deferred and observed, painting nothing, the first in view loading on the first observation and the second on scrolling, with their `load` events; images in a scroller loading within a scrollport of its clip; changing `loading` to eager, an image already in the memory cache, no scripting, and removing the source). The whole Booey suite passes (2702 cases; 7 expected failures); Krystal.UI's 103 cases pass except the filters golden, off by 26 pixels on battery power.

## The drag image (B10d, 2026-10-26)

Part B10d of drag and drop (*B10 plan* in `docs/booey/ROADMAP.md`): the image a drag shows under the cursor (a snapshot of the dragged element or the selection, a link's label, an image's own image, or the one the page set with `setDragImage()`), and Krystal.UI drawing it. Read in full: `platform/DragImage.h`, `.cpp`, `platform/skia/DragImageSkia.cpp`, `platform/cairo/DragImageCairo.cpp`, the old Windows port's `platform/win/DragImageWin.cpp` and `WebCoreTextRenderer.cpp` (from the commit before `adefaa9ed9f8`, for links' labels, the user's decision), `page/FrameSnapshotting.h`, `.cpp`, `platform/graphics/StringTruncator.h`, `.cpp`; `DataTransfer`'s drag image (`setDragImage`, `updateDragImage`, `createDragImage`, `dragImageElement`, `hasDragImage`, `DragImageLoader`, `moveDragState`); `Pasteboard::setDragImage` (`PasteboardGLib.cpp`) and `StaticPasteboard`'s; `DragController`'s drag images (`startDrag`, `doImageDrag`, `doSystemDrag`, `dragLocForDHTMLDrag`, `maxDragImageSize`, `shouldUseCachedImageForDragImage` and the constants in `DragControllerGLib.cpp`); `EventHandler::handleDrag`'s default image; `LocalFrameView::setNodeToDraw`, `paintContentsForSnapshot` and `paintContents`'s node to draw; `RenderObject::paintingRootRect`, `addAbsoluteRectForLayer`.

| WebKit | Verdict | Krystal | CMake | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|

See *Differences*. |
| `page/FrameSnapshotting.h`, `.cpp` | `port*` | `Page/FrameSnapshotting.hpp`, `src/Page/FrameSnapshotting.cpp` (new) | on | No pixel format or colour space in the options (image buffers record display lists); no `estimatedBackgroundColorForRange` (text indicators'). |
| `platform/graphics/StringTruncator.h`, `.cpp` | `port` | `Graphics/StringTruncator.hpp`, `src/Graphics/StringTruncator.cpp` (new) | on | Over UTF-8: lengths and the 2048 limit are bytes, and cuts fall on grapheme clusters. iOS's whitespace stripping isn't ported. |
| `dom/DataTransfer.h`, `.cpp` (drag image) | `port` | `DOM/DataTransfer.hpp`, `src/DOM/DataTransfer.cpp` | on | `DragImageLoader` is in the source; the FIXMEs went. |
| `platform/Pasteboard.h`, `platform/glib/PasteboardGLib.cpp`, `platform/StaticPasteboard.h` (`setDragImage`) | `port` | `Platform/Pasteboard.hpp`, `StaticPasteboard.hpp`, `src/Platform/Pasteboard.cpp` | on | Does nothing, as GLib's: a drag keeps the image it started with. |

| `rendering/RenderObject.h`, `.cpp` (`paintingRootRect`, `addAbsoluteRectForLayer`) | `port` | `Rendering/RenderObject.hpp`, `src/...` | on | |

**Bugs fixed:**
- `StringTruncator`'s `leftTruncateToBuffer` dropped the grapheme boundary it looked up (`boundedTextBreakFollowing`'s result was unused), so a left truncation could start inside a cluster; over UTF-8 that would cut a code point. It starts at the boundary at or after the cut.
- `anchorPointForLinkDragImage` divided integers, so the anchor's y was always 0 (and a zero-height image divided by zero). It divides floats, and a zero height gives 0.

**Added (upstream API):** `DragImageRef`, `DragImage`, `DragImageData`, `DragImageSize`, `FitDragImageToMaxSize`, `ScaleDragImage`, `PlatformAdjustDragImageForDeviceScaleFactor`, `DissolveDragImageToFraction`, `CreateDragImageFromImage`, `CreateDragImageIconForCachedImageFilename`, `CreateDragImageForNode`, `CreateDragImageForSelection`, `CreateDragImageForLink`, `DragOffsetForLinkDragImage`, `AnchorPointForLinkDragImage`; `SnapshotFlags`, `SnapshotOptions`, `SnapshotFrameRect`, `SnapshotFrameRectWithClip`, `SnapshotNode`, `SnapshotSelection`; `StringTruncator`; `DataTransfer::SetDragImage`, `CreateDragImage`, `UpdateDragImage`, `DragImageElement`, `HasDragImage`; `Pasteboard::SetDragImage`; `DragItem::Image`, `ImageAnchorPoint`; `DragController::MaxDragImageSize`, `MaxOriginalImageArea`, `DragIconRightInset`, `DragIconBottomInset`, `DragImageAlpha`, `DoImageDrag`, `ShouldUseCachedImageForDragImage`; `LocalFrameView::SetNodeToDraw`, `PaintContentsForSnapshot`, `SelectionInSnapshot`, `CoordinateSpaceForSnapshot`; `RenderObject::PaintingRootRect`, `AddAbsoluteRectForLayer`.
**Differences:**
- Drag images are image buffers, which record display lists rather than pixels: a snapshot is the drag image itself (not turned into a bitmap, so not oriented, as on Skia and Cairo, which ignore the orientation too); scaling one redraws it at the new size rather than resampling it; fading one draws it at the fraction's alpha into a new buffer; an image's drag image draws the image into a buffer at its size.
- Links' labels are the old Windows port's (the user's decision, 2026-10-26; GLib has none): a grey rounded rectangle with the link's text in bold over its URL in the system's small caption font, each cut to fit 200px with an ellipsis. Text of more than one direction is drawn in logical order (FIXME: the port's `drawBidiText`), and the label is drawn at one device pixel a pixel, then scaled by the device scale factor (losslessly, as it's a display list). Upstream's Windows label was opaque; Krystal.UI fades it (below).
- No icons for dragged images' files (`createDragImageIconForCachedImageFilename` gives none, as GLib; the response's suggested filename isn't parsed either, FIXME), no colour swatches (colour drags aren't ported), no ranges' or images' drag images (`createDragImageForRange` and `createDragImageForImage` are only the Mac's and iOS's) and no text indicators or visible paths (FIXMEs).
- `ScopedNodeDragEnabler` only updates the layout: elements have no drag state, as `:-webkit-drag` isn't supported.
- The page has no device scale factor of its own: the document's is used. Snapshots ignore the page's scale (FIXME: pages that delegate scaling).
- Krystal.UI draws the drag item's image under the cursor, over the page and any overlay, offset as the page put it (the drag location less the press) and in CSS pixels (its size over the device scale factor). Selections' and images' images are faded by Booey (`DragImageAlpha`, as upstream); the page's own images (an element, or the one it set) and links' labels, which upstream leaves to the platform, are drawn at the same alpha (the user's decision, 2026-10-26), so every drag image is translucent. As GLib's pasteboard, `setDragImage()` after the drag started doesn't change the image.
Tests: `tests/Graphics/StringTruncator.cpp` (1 case / 20 assertions: strings that fit, right, centre and left truncation, clipping to a character and a word, grapheme clusters kept whole); `tests/Platform/DragImage.cpp` (3 cases / 43 assertions: snapshots of a node with its descendants' layers, a node that isn't rendered, a frame rect, the selection; scaling, fading, fitting and the device scale factor; nodes', selections' and links' images, links' offsets and anchors); `tests/DOM/DataTransfer.cpp` (+1 case: which data transfers take a drag image, an element's snapshot and its location, an image out of a document without its image, `dragstart`'s image moved to the drag); `tests/Page/DragController.cpp` (+1 case: an element's image under the press, the page's image from `dragstart`, a link's label below the cursor, a selection's). The whole Booey suite passes (2788 cases). Krystal.UI: `tests/DragAndDrop.cpp` (+1 section and +1 GPU case: the image follows the cursor, faded, until the drop; painted under the cursor at three quarters opacity); 120 cases pass.

## Dragging within a page (B10c, 2026-10-25)

Part B10c of drag and drop (*B10 plan* in `docs/booey/ROADMAP.md`): drags that start in a page (draggable elements, links, images and the selection), with their events at the source and the targets, the operation agreed between them, what a drop does by default, the drag caret, autoscrolling while dragging, and Krystal.UI running the drag. **Bugs fixed:** none found.
**Added (upstream API):** `DragDestinationAction`, `DragSourceAction`, `DragOperation` and their `Any*`, `MayExtendDragSession`, `HasNonDefaultPasteboardData`, `DragHandlingMethod`; `DragState`; `DragClient`, `EmptyDragClient`; `DragItem`; `DragData`, `DragApplicationFlags`; `DragEvent`, `DragEventInit`, `Event::IsDragEvent` and the drag event names; `DragController`, `IsDraggableLink`; `MoveSelectionCommand`; `EventHandler`'s drag state (`GetDragState`, `DraggedElement`), `UpdateDragAndDrop`, `CancelDragAndDrop`, `PerformDragAndDrop`, `UpdateDragStateAfterEditDragIfNeeded`, `EventMayStartDrag`, `DidStartDrag`, `DragCancelled`, `DragSourceEndedAt`, `CanDropCurrentlyDraggedImageAsFile`, the hysteresis constants, `TextDragDelay`, `CapturesDragging`; `DataTransfer::CreateForDrag`, `CreateForDragStartEvent`, `CreateForDrop`, `CreateForUpdatingDropTarget`, `DropEffectIsUninitialized`, `SourceOperationMask`, `DestinationOperationMask` and their setters, `SetDragHasStarted`, `MoveDragState`; `Pasteboard::CreateForDragAndDrop`, `Create(DragData)`, `Write(PasteboardImage)`, `PasteboardImage`; `DragCaretController`; `Page::GetDragController`, `GetDragCaretController` and `Create`'s drag client; `AutoscrollController::UpdateDragAndDrop`; `HitTestResult::IsSelected`, `AltDisplayString`, `GetImage`, `ImageRect`, `AbsoluteImageURL`, `AbsoluteLinkURL`, `TextContent`; `Element::AbsoluteLinkURL`; `LocalFrame::VisiblePositionForPoint`, `DocumentAtPoint`; `Editor::CopyURL`, `WriteImageToPasteboard`, `IgnoreSelectionChangeForScope`; `InputType::ReceiveDroppedFiles`, `FileInputType::FilesChosen`, `HTMLInputElement::ReceiveDroppedFiles`, `CanReceiveDroppedFiles`, `SetCanReceiveDroppedFiles`.
**Differences:**
- Booey has one frame and no remote frames: subframes' drags (`contentFrameForNode`), remote frames' user input data, the root view's coordinates (the frame's window coordinates stand for them) and the root frame's identifier aren't ported.
- Drag images came with B10d (*The drag image*).
- No security origins: whether the document under the mouse may take the initiator's data (`canReceiveDragData`), whether a page may display the link it drags (`canDisplay`), and images' restricted origins (`restrictedOriginForImageData`, so `CanDropCurrentlyDraggedImageAsFile` is always true) are FIXMEs.
- The non-standard `webkitdropzone` attribute (`findDropZone`, `hasDropZoneType`) isn't ported.
- No colour drags (dragging a colour input and dropping colours, with colours on the pasteboard), dropped image placeholders, attachments, models, data detector links, image overlays or plugin documents (FIXMEs, or Cocoa's).
- The drag events' modifiers are none (FIXME: upstream reads the keys held from the platform); the copy key comes in the drag data's flags. `TextDragDelay` is zero, as off the Mac, and `eventActivatedView` and `eventLoopHandleMouseDragged` are the Mac's.
- Dropped URLs load with the frame loader as a request from user input, without upstream's external URL policy (FIXME). `IsDraggableLink` keeps Booey's test for HTML links (an `href` and not editable, FIXME: the editable link behavior setting).
- `AutoscrollForDragAndDropEnabled` is on (the user's decision, 2026-10-25), where upstream's default is off and only iOS turns it on.
- Upstream declares `DragController::dragCancelled` without defining it; it isn't ported.
- `DragController::DragSourceAction()` is `GetDragSourceAction()`, and `dragOperation(DragData)` is `DragOperationFor` (the names would hide the types).
- File inputs take dropped files without image transcoding (the Mac's); `SetCanReceiveDroppedFiles` doesn't update the renderer, as file inputs don't draw their button yet.
- The accessibility notifications of drags and the drag source (`onDraggingStarted`, `onDragElementChanged` and the others) aren't ported (FIXME: accessibility).
- Krystal.UI runs the drag itself (the B10 plan), as the GTK host's drag source and drop target do: its `DragClient` keeps the drag's `SelectionData` and what the source allows; the view's mouse moves become `DragEnteredOrUpdated` over the page and `DragExited` off it, the release `PerformDragOperation` (when the page would take the drop), then `DragEnded` and `DragSourceEndedAt` with the operation done, as `WebPage::dragEnded`; Escape and losing focus cancel; Ctrl is the copy key; the cursor is OLE's for the operation (the user's decision). The page doesn't see the release (as with a system drag), and the drag's positions aren't offset by the drag offset (WebKit adds it for the Mac's image positions). Krystal.PAL captures the mouse while a button is held (the user's decision), so a drag follows the mouse out of the window and a release there cancels it.
Tests: `tests/Page/DragController.cpp` (9 cases / 104 assertions: an element drag's events in order with the hysteresis, the data written in `dragstart` read in `drop` and protected in `dragover`, and `dragend`'s drop effect; what doesn't start a drag (unselected text selects, a client allowing nothing, a cancelled `dragstart`); link drags' hysteresis, URL and markup; refused, left and unallowed drops; `effectAllowed`'s values; moving the selection within editable content, copying it with the copy key, text from elsewhere, the drag caret and its renderer, a cancelled `textInput`; text into a text field, files into a file input and too many for one that takes one; URLs over static and editable content; draggable elements that can't be selected). The whole Booey suite passes (2782 cases). Krystal.UI: `tests/DragAndDrop.cpp` (1 case / 28 assertions: a drag through the view: dropping on a target that takes it, moving text into editable content, leaving and coming back, Escape, losing focus, with the cursors); 119 cases pass. Krystal.PAL's capture and cursors aren't driven by tests.

## DataTransfer and the clipboard (B10b, 2026-10-25)

Part B10b of drag and drop (*B10 plan* in `docs/booey/ROADMAP.md`): `DataTransfer` and its items, the pasteboards behind it, clipboard events carrying their data, and pastes' input events carrying theirs. Read in full: `dom/DataTransfer.h`, `.cpp`, `DataTransferItem.h`, `.cpp`, `DataTransferItemList.h`, `.cpp`, `ClipboardEvent.h`, `.cpp`; `InputEvent`'s data transfer; `platform/Pasteboard.h`, `.cpp`, `StaticPasteboard.h`, `.cpp`, `PasteboardCustomData.h`, `.cpp`, `PasteboardStrategy.h`; GLib's pasteboard (`platform/glib/PasteboardGLib.cpp`, `SelectionData.h`, `.cpp`, `platform/gtk/PasteboardGtk.cpp`, `platform/wpe/PasteboardWPE.cpp`); `editing/WebContentReader.h`, `.cpp`, `editing/glib/WebContentReaderGLib.cpp`, `editing/WebCorePasteboardFileReader.h`, `.cpp`; `editing/glib/EditorGLib.cpp`; `Editor`'s `createDataTransferForClipboardEvent`, `dispatchClipboardEvent`, `performCutOrCopy`, `paste` and `pasteAsPlainText`; `CompositeEditCommand` and `ReplaceSelectionCommand`'s `inputEventDataTransfer`; `editing/markup.cpp`'s `createPageForSanitizingWebContent`, `sanitizeMarkup` and `sanitizedMarkupForFragmentInDocument`; `Document::originIdentifierForPasteboard`; the GTK and WPE hosts' `WebPasteboardProxy` (`typesSafeForDOMToReadAndWrite`, `writeCustomData`, `writeToClipboard`) for Krystal.UI's strategy; `platform/win/ClipboardUtilitiesWin.cpp`'s `markupToCFHTML` and `extractMarkupFromCFHTML` for Krystal.PAL.

**Bugs fixed:** `Markup.cpp`'s composed tree walk asked for the slot of any node, which asserted on nodes that can't be slotted (comments, doctypes); upstream's lookup returns null for them. Nothing serialised the composed tree until copying did.
**Added (upstream API):** `DataTransfer` (its modes and store, `Create`, `CreateForCopyAndPaste`, `CreateForInputEvent`, `DropEffect`, `EffectAllowed` and their setters, `Items`, `Types`, `TypesForItemList`, `Files`, `ClearData`, `GetData`, `GetDataForItem`, `SetData`, `SetDataFromItemList`, `MakeInvalidForSecurity`, `CanReadTypes`, `CanReadData`, `CanWriteData`, `HasFileOfType`, `HasStringOfType`, `CommitToPasteboard`, `DidAddFileToItemList`, `UpdateFileList`); `DataTransferItem` and `DataTransferItemList`; `ClipboardEvent::ClipboardData` and its init's; `InputEvent::GetDataTransfer` and its init's; `Pasteboard`'s types, origin, custom data, readers (web content, files), URL and web content writing, file content state and `ReadBuffer`; `PasteboardWebContent`, `PasteboardURL`, `PasteboardWebContentReader`, `PasteboardFileReader`, `PlainTextURLReadingPolicy`, `WebContentReadingPolicy`; `SelectionData`; `StaticPasteboard`; `PasteboardCustomData`; `WebContentReader`, `WebContentMarkupReader`, `FrameWebContentReader`; `Editor::WriteSelectionToPasteboard`, `WebContentFromPasteboard`, and `DispatchClipboardEvent` with a data transfer; `CompositeEditCommand::InputEventDataTransfer`; `CreatePageForSanitizingWebContent`, `SanitizeMarkup`, `SanitizedMarkupForFragmentInDocument`, `MSOListQuirks`; `Document::OriginIdentifierForPasteboard`.
**Differences:**
- The pasteboard follows GLib's model (the user's decision, 2026-10-25): a pasteboard is the system clipboard, read and written through the host's strategy by type (`Types`, `ReadTextFromClipboard`, `ReadFilePathsFromClipboard`, `ReadBufferFromClipboard`, `WriteToClipboard` with a `SelectionData`, `ClearClipboard`, `ChangeCount`, `TypesSafeForDOMToReadAndWrite`, `WriteCustomData`), or a `SelectionData` (a drag's data, from B10c). The old `ReadDocumentFragment` (Windows' `documentFragment` of plain text) went: pasting reads web content through a `WebContentReader`, as GTK and WPE do. Pasteboard contexts, names other than `CLIPBOARD`, the primary selection and the strategy's calls by item index (the async clipboard API's) aren't ported.
- Custom pasteboard data is always on (the user's decision; it's on in WebKit for Windows, GTK and WPE), so there's no setting and none of its disabled paths (`typesForLegacyUnsafeBindings`, `readAllStrings` of the legacy types). Pages' own types travel in a private clipboard format with the writer's origin, and HTML a page writes, or reads from another origin, is sanitised in a staging page, as upstream.
- Documents have no security origins, so `OriginIdentifierForPasteboard` is always upstream's identifier for an opaque origin (`null:` and a UUID): a page reads back the custom types it copied, but no other document does.
- `PasteboardCustomData`'s serialised form is its own (a version, the origin, and each type with its same-origin string), not WTF's persistence coder's; it carries the same data.
- File access follows Cocoa's rule (the user's decision): files are readable from pastes and file drags, not from drags of page content (`!forDrag() || forFileDrag()`), where upstream's other ports allow none (bug 271957).
- Link decoration filtering (`applyLinkDecorationFiltering`) and the quirk adding `application/x-moz-file` aren't ported.
- `SetEffectAllowed` didn't ignore unknown values (that needed `DragOperation`); it does since B10c.
- `DataTransferItemList` forwards its references to its data transfer, as upstream, but isn't a context destruction observer; it keeps its document weakly.
- `GetAsString` takes a function for the callback and queues it on the DOM manipulation task source.
- `WebContentReader::ReadFilePath` makes a file URL from the path (`URL::FileURLWithFileSystemPath`), where upstream parses the path as a URL (POSIX paths); `WebContentMarkupReader` doesn't remove subresource URL attributes (FIXME: URL attributes), and nothing prefers images' types (FIXME).
- `SanitizeMarkup` returns none when the staging page has no document (upstream's null string), takes a function rather than an optional one, and clears the staging page's document when done.
Tests: `tests/DOM/DataTransfer.cpp` (5 cases / 102 assertions: data by normalised types and in order, what's written for other applications and sanitised, the store's modes, drop effects, input events' data; items with the data, files and file items, strings given in a task, read-only items; files on the clipboard listed but their paths not exposed; custom data's serialisation; URI lists and URLs in selection data). `tests/Editing/Editor.cpp` gains *clipboard events' data* (cancelled copies committing what listeners wrote, uncancelled copies, the events before copying, paste listeners reading the clipboard, rich text pasted as markup, a page reading back its custom types and another not, pastes' input events' data, files given to paste listeners) and *input events in text fields have no data transfer*; its copy tests check the markup and origin written. `tests/Editing/EditorTestUtils.hpp`'s strategy is a clipboard in memory. Krystal.UI's view tests use a clipboard in memory on the new strategy, and check that copying writes markup.

**Bugs fixed:** none.
**Added (upstream API):** `Blob` (its constructors, `Type`, `Size`, `IsFile`, `Slice`, `IsValidContentType`, `NormalizedContentType`, `MemoryCost`, and `Bytes` and `Text` for its `bytes()` and `text()`), `BlobPartVariant`, `BlobPropertyBag` and `EndingType`; `File` (`Create` from a path, from parts, from a blob and from a file; `Path`, `Name`, `LastModified`, `LastModifiedOverride`, `ContentTypeForFile`, `IsDirectory`); `FileList`; `BlobDataItem` and `BlobData`; `MIMETypeRegistry::MIMETypeForExtension` and `DefaultMIMEType`; `FileInputType`'s file list (`Files`, `SetFiles`, `FirstElementPathForInputValue`, clearing on `SetValue`, `SaveFormControlState` and `RestoreFormControlState`, files in `AppendFormData`, `DirAutoUsesValue`); `HTMLInputElement::Files` and `SetFiles`; `DOMFormData`'s file entries (`Append` and `Set` with a blob); `CustomElementFormValue`'s file; `FormDataElement`, `FormData::AppendFile`, `AppendFileRange`, `Elements` and multipart file values.
**Differences:**
- No blob registry or blob URLs: a blob holds its data (`BlobData`, upstream's canonical list of data and file ranges) itself, and slicing and sizing are `BlobData`'s (the registry's upstream). Neither is a script execution context or an active DOM object.
- Reading is synchronous (the user's decision, 2026-10-25): `Bytes()` and `Text()` read on the spot and return the exception a failed read rejects with (`NotFoundError` for a missing file, `NotReadableError` otherwise), where upstream's `bytes()`, `text()`, `arrayBuffer()` and `stream()` load asynchronously; no `FileReader` or streams. `Text()` drops a byte order mark and replaces invalid bytes, as UTF-8 decode does.
- Files keep their path as a string and aren't checked against their modification time when read.
- `MIMETypeForExtension` has upstream's Windows table only; the registry's content types for other extensions (upstream's fallback) are a FIXME, so most other extensions have no type.
- `File::Create` from a file with a name takes it as `Maybe` (upstream's null string), so the two overloads for blobs and files don't clash.
- A file input's files are set from C++ (`SetFiles`, which fires `input` and `change` unless set by script) or restored with the form's state; the chooser the host shows is a FIXME, as before.
- `FormData::Flatten()` leaves files out, as upstream; nothing reads them yet (Booey has no network loader).
Tests: `tests/FileAPI/Blob.cpp` (3 cases / 87 assertions: parts in order, types, native line endings, slices across items and from the end, decoding; files on disk with their names, types, sizes, times and slices, a file that's gone, a directory, files from parts, blobs and files; file lists). `tests/HTML/FileInputType.cpp` (2 cases / 55 assertions: only file inputs have files, events when they change or not, the fake path, required, clearing by the value, saving and restoring; form data entries with and without files, multipart bodies with file elements, URL-encoded names, blobs' bytes, setting entries). `tests/HTML/ElementInternals.cpp` gains *they submit files*. Changed to read entries' strings: `tests/HTML/FormController.cpp`, `HTMLFormElement.cpp`, `ElementInternals.cpp`, and Krystal.UI's `tests/View.cpp`.

| GTK's `WebPage` and `WebEditorClient` (input methods), `InputMethodFilter`, the web view's composition key presses | `port*` | `Krystal.UI/EditorClient.hpp`, `src/EditorClient.cpp`, `View.hpp`, `src/View.cpp`, `Input.hpp`, `src/Input.cpp` | Krystal.UI | See *Differences*. |

**Added (upstream API):** `Element::ShouldUseInputMethod()` and its overrides (`InputType::ShouldUseInputMethod()` for inputs); `EditorClient::SetInputMethodState()`. Krystal.UI: the editor client's input method hooks (as GTK's `WebPage` and editor client: cancelling the composition the selection leaves, the input method's keydowns, whether the focus takes text); `View::SetComposition()`, `ConfirmComposition()`, `InsertText()`, `AcceptsTextInput()`, `TextInputRect()` and `SetCompositionDiscardedHandler()`; `input::InputMethodKeyboardEvent()`, `TextInputEvent()` and `CompositionUnderlines()`.
**Differences:**
- `SetInputMethodState()` is called wherever the focused element changes (`DesignateFocusedArea`, with null as the old element loses focus and then with the new one), and when the focused element is removed; upstream calls it from `FocusController::setFocusedElement` alone (Booey has no focus controller), so removing the focused element left the input method on.
- As on GTK, the keys the input method takes don't reach the page; each change to the composition comes as a key press it handled (`keydown` with key code 229, key `Unidentified`), carrying the composition or the committed text. The plan had the keys themselves go out as key code 229 (as other engines do on Windows); that would send two for each.
- The selection set with a composition is a caret at the input method's caret; GTK sends a one-character range there.
- The page confirms its composition as the mouse (or a pen or a touch) presses and as the window loses focus, and asks the host to drop the input method's (GTK confirms with the input method's text and resets it); a host's `CompleteComposition()` isn't used, so its result can't arrive after the focus moved. When the selection leaves the composition otherwise, it's cancelled with its text left (`WebPage::didChangeSelection`), and the host drops the input method's too.
- Characters without a key press are typed as a `keypress` with them alone (decision 3), as Windows' `WM_CHAR` is upstream.
- No input purpose or hints (`inputmode`, `autocapitalize`, spell checking): `inputmode` is out of B9.
Tests: `tests/Editing/Composition.cpp` gains *Editor client: the input method follows the focus* (6 cases / 85 assertions pass): text fields, text areas and editable content take it, password fields, checkboxes and other elements don't, and blurring or removing the focused element turns it off. Krystal.UI: `Krystal.UI.Tests/tests/InputMethod.cpp`, *View: the input method* (39 assertions): the focus, the rect, keys the input method took, composing and committing through key code 229, emptying, text without a key press, and the composition confirmed on blur and on a press, and cancelled as the selection leaves it.

## IME composition (B9a, 2026-10-25)

Part B9a of IME composition (*B9 plan* in `docs/booey/ROADMAP.md`): the text an input method composes, in the editor, the events and the painting. Graphs from `dom/CompositionEvent.h`, `editing/CompositionUnderline.h` and `editing/CompositionHighlight.h` (headers-only, following `css/`, `style/`, `dom/` and `editing/`): the three files are new, the rest is ported. Read in full besides: `Editor`'s composition (`setComposition` both ways, `confirmComposition`, `cancelComposition`, `confirmOrCancelCompositionAndNotifyClient`, `cancelCompositionIfSelectionIsInvalid`, `compositionRange`, `getCompositionSelection`, `selectComposition`, `insertTextForConfirmedComposition`, `setIgnoreSelectionChanges`, `respondToChangedSelection`, `firstRectForRange`, `handleInputMethodKeydown`, `didDispatchInputMethodKeydown`), `EventHandler::internalKeyEvent`'s input method path, `KeyboardEvent`'s `isComposing`, `PlatformKeyboardEvent`'s input method fields (and GTK's `disambiguateKeyDownEvent`), `TextBoxPainter`'s composition painting, `RenderObject::absoluteTextQuads` and `RenderText::absoluteQuadsForRange`, `TemporarySelectionChange`, `FrameSelection::setSelectionWithoutUpdatingAppearance`'s call to the editor, and the clients that answer the editor (the GTK editor client's input method keydowns, `WebPage::didChangeSelection` cancelling a composition the selection left).

**Bugs fixed:**
- Typing after a no-break space left the caret (and the typing command's ending selection) a byte too far. Rebalancing whitespace turns a no-break space (two bytes in UTF-8, one unit in UTF-16) into a space (one byte), and the commands kept offsets taken before. The next keystroke asserted a position past the end of its text node, and a composition after one was recorded a byte late. Rebalancing now returns the run it replaced (`WhitespaceRebalance`), which moves positions across it; typing, deleting, replacing and `RebalanceWhitespace()` use it.
- Upstream's `getCompositionSelection` gives the selection's end as the start's offset less the composition's end; it's now the end's offset less the composition's start.

**Added (upstream API):** `CompositionEvent` and its init dictionary, with `compositionstart`, `compositionupdate` and `compositionend`; `CompositionUnderline`, `CompositionHighlight`; `Editor`'s composition (above), `InsertTextForConfirmedComposition()`, `SetIgnoreSelectionChanges()`, `IgnoreSelectionChanges()`, `RespondToChangedSelection()`, `FirstRectForRange()`, `HandleInputMethodKeydown()`, `DidDispatchInputMethodKeydown()`, `CloseTyping()`; the editor client's hooks (above); `PlatformKeyboardEvent::HandledByInputMethod()`, `PreeditUnderlines()`, `PreeditSelectionRangeStart()` and `PreeditSelectionRangeLength()`; `Event::IsCompositionEvent()`, `IsDefaultEventHandlerIgnored()` and `SetIsDefaultEventHandlerIgnored()`; `RenderObject::AbsoluteTextQuads()`, `RenderObjectBoundingRectBehavior`; `RenderText::AbsoluteQuadsForRange()`.
**Differences:**
- Composition offsets (the underlines, the selection within the text) are in the text's UTF-8 code units, as Booey's DOM offsets are; the host converts an input method's UTF-16 offsets.
- The host's custom highlights and annotations (Cocoa's inline predictions and writing suggestions) are out: `SetComposition()` takes neither, and the painter has no custom highlight foreground or rounded fills. The redesigned text cursor's rounded underlines are Cocoa's and out.
- Undo doesn't cancel the composition: upstream does so only on iOS. Elsewhere the host cancels it when the selection leaves it, as Booey's hosts do from `RespondToChangedSelection()` (upstream's web page does).
- The input method's result rides on the key press, as on GTK (`handledByInputMethod`, the preedit). The keydown then goes out as key code 229 with no default handling and no `keypress`, and the editor client applies the result after it (`DidDispatchInputMethodKeydown()`). A composing `keypress` goes to the editor client, not the page. Krystal.UI's client is still empty; B9c fills it.
- `createEvent("compositionevent")` isn't supported: `Document::CreateEvent()` makes plain events for every interface still.
- No user typing gesture (`UserTypingGestureIndicator`) or accessibility notifications, as elsewhere.
Tests: `tests/Editing/Composition.cpp`: 5 cases / 74 assertions pass: starting, updating, confirming (with its own text or another), cancelling and emptying a composition in editable content, with its events in order, the underlines, the selection within it, the selection leaving it, undo and its rect; recomposing a selection; composing after a no-break space; a text field; keys an input method handled (key code 229, `isComposing`, the preedit and the confirmed text). `tests/Editing/TypingCommand.cpp` checks the caret after a rebalanced no-break space. Krystal.UI: page goldens `composition` (clause underlines: thin, thick, and in their own colour) and `composition-fill`.

## Close requests without Escape (B8d, 2026-10-25)

Part B8d of gamepads (*B8 plan* in `docs/booey/ROADMAP.md`) is Krystal.UI's mapping of the pad onto the page (*B8d as built* there); its one change in Booey is here. The pad's B is a close request with no key event behind it, which the standard allows (user agents may treat other actions as close requests), so `CloseWatcherManager` gets the standard's *process close watchers* on its own.

**Bugs fixed:**
- Upstream's `makeGamepadVisible` fired `gamepadconnected` at every registered window, not just the set given: windows that already saw the pads got the event again when a blind one was shown them. Booey fires at the set given.
- Upstream never sets a disconnected gamepad's `connected` to false (`setConnected` is never called), so the `gamepaddisconnected` event's gamepad still said it was connected; the standard sets it to false. Booey does.
- `Gamepad.timestamp` was the monotonic clock's seconds; the standard has it in milliseconds from the time origin, which Booey returns.
- `GamepadHapticActuator::stopEffects` dereferenced its gamepad without checking its weak pointer (an actuator outliving its gamepad); Booey checks.
- Booey's `Document::Hidden()` was always true: the visibility state was a member that defaulted to hidden and was never set, so haptics always preempted. It's now upstream's: hidden without a page; the page's visibility is visible until hosts report it (a FIXME).
- `EventTargetAlgorithms::RemoveEventListener` now reads the listener's type before erasing it, as erasing may drop its last reference (found by the new hook).

**Added (upstream API):** `PlatformGamepad`, `GamepadProvider`, `GamepadProviderClient`, `EventMakesGamepadsVisible`, `EmptyGamepadProvider`, `GamepadButtonRole` and the standard layout's constants, `KnownGamepad`; `GamepadHapticEffectType`, `GamepadHapticEffectTypeSet`, `GamepadEffectParameters`, `GamepadButton`, `Gamepad`, `GamepadEventInit`, `GamepadEvent`, `GamepadHapticActuator` (`Type`), `GamepadHapticsResult`, `GamepadManager`, `NavigatorGamepad`; `Navigator::GetGamepads()`, `Document()`, `GamepadsIfExists()`; `LocalDOMWindow::TimeOrigin()`, `NavigatorIfExists()`, `ongamepadconnected`, `ongamepaddisconnected`; `Event::IsGamepadEvent()`; `TaskSource::Gamepad`; `EventTarget::DidAddEventListener()`, `DidRemoveEventListener()`.
**Differences:** as in the table. `GamepadHapticActuator::effects` (the standard's list of effect types) is missing upstream too. Krystal.UI's provider, which isn't a port, is described in *B8c as built* in `ROADMAP.md`.
Tests: `tests/Modules/Gamepad/Gamepad.cpp` (`Gamepad: pads appear after a button press`, `Gamepad: connection events`, `Gamepad: a window's listeners alone monitor the pads`, `Gamepad: haptics`): 4 cases / 59 assertions pass; Krystal.UI: `tests/GamepadProvider.cpp` (`GamepadProvider: pads from the platform layer`, `GamepadProvider: pads connecting while monitored`): 2 cases / 38 assertions pass.

## Gestures and touch scrolling (B7d, 2026-10-25)

Part B7d of pointer and touch input (*B7 plan* in `docs/booey/ROADMAP.md`): touches that pages leave alone pan, fling, tap, long press and pinch, which needs page scale. The render view's page scale transform, the background under a scale below 1, the root layer's unscaled bounds, the overlap map's scaled clip. |

**Bugs fixed:**
- A touch's pointer events went on after `pointercancel`: upstream never stops them (its non-iOS hosts never cancel a touch's pointer, and iOS's stops sending the touches), but the standard fires nothing more for a cancelled pointer. `DispatchEventForTouchAtIndex` drops them until the touch ends.

**Added (upstream API):** `EventHandler::SendContextMenuEvent()`, `SelectClosestContextualWordFromHitTestResult()`, `SelectClosestContextualWordOrLinkFromHitTestResult()`; `Page::SetPageScaleFactor()`, `PageScaleFactor()`; `LocalFrame::FrameScaleFactor()`, `DeviceOrPageScaleFactorChanged()`; `HistoryItem::PageScaleFactor()`, `SetPageScaleFactor()`.
**Differences:** as in the table. B7b's forgetting of ended touches moved: their pointers are forgotten at the next touch event rather than at their own, so the host's tap after a touch lifts still sees whether its `pointerdown` was cancelled (upstream, iOS's host forgets them once its tap is done). Taps don't snap the caret to a word boundary (`wordBoundaryForPositionWithoutCrossingLine` needs the visible units' granularity queries: a FIXME). Upstream's wheel scrolling (and so touch scrolling) doesn't divide by the page scale for boxes inside the page, so a pan scrolls an inner box twice as far as the finger moves at scale 2; kept.
**Host:** Krystal.UI's view sends `contextmenu` after a press of the right button (and the pen's barrel button), as WebKit's host does. Its touches make gestures where the page doesn't cancel them (`touchstart`, a `touchmove` before the gesture starts, or `touchend` for a tap) and the used `touch-action` where they began allows: a touch that moves 10 pixels pans (`pointercancel`, then `HandleTouchScroll()` from where it began, along the axes `touch-action` allows; a direction it doesn't allow leaves the touch to the page), and flings on if it lifts moving (its velocity over the last 100ms, decaying with a time constant of 0.325s, as `Update` runs; a touch stops it and can't tap); one that lifts sooner taps (a mouse move, press and release of type `OneFingerTap` from the touch's pointer, so the click is the touch's and a cancelled `pointerdown` stops the compatibility mouse events; two within 500ms and 20 pixels double click); one held 500ms is a long press, asking for a context menu as it lifts (`contextmenu`), as Windows' press and hold and WPE's host do (upstream drops a `contextmenu` while a touch is down); two pinch (`pointercancel` for both, then the page's scale follows the touches' distance, from 1 to 5, keeping the document point between them under them).
Tests: `tests/Page/EventHandler.cpp` (`EventHandler: contextmenu`: 1 case / 12 assertions), `tests/Page/Page.cpp` (`Page: page scale`, `Page: page scale paints the content scaled`: 2 cases / 21 assertions), `tests/Page/LocalFrameViewScrolling.cpp` (`LocalFrameView: a touch's pan scrolls`: 1 case / 17 assertions); Krystal.UI's `View: gestures`: 1 case / 32 assertions pass.

## Pointer lock (B7c, 2026-10-25)

Part B7c of pointer and touch input (*B7 plan* in `docs/booey/ROADMAP.md`): pages lock the pointer to an element, and the host hides and confines the cursor and reports the mouse's movement. Graph from `page/PointerLockController.h` (headers-only, following `page/` and `dom/`): the new files are the controller and `dom/PointerLockOptions.h`; the rest is already in Booey or out of scope. Read in full: those, their IDL (`Element+PointerLock.idl`, `Document+PointerLock.idl`, `DocumentOrShadowRoot+PointerLock.idl`), and the call sites: `Element::requestPointerLock` and `removedFromAncestor`, `Document::exitPointerLock`, the document's detaching and its back/forward cache state, `TreeScope::pointerLockElement`, `ChromeClient`'s lock and unlock, `LocalDOMWindow`'s `alert`, `confirm` and `prompt`, `PointerCaptureController::setPointerCapture`, and `EventHandler`'s mouse, wheel and key handling.

| WebKit | Verdict | Krystal | CMake | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `page/PointerLockController.h`, `.cpp` | `port*` | `Page/PointerLockController.hpp`, `src/...` (new) | on | tested. The promises are callbacks (`PointerLockCallback`, settled as microtasks). The user gesture is the window's transient activation. The sandbox check is a FIXME (no sandboxed frames). Forcing the cursor visible on unlock is dropped (Booey's chrome client has no cursor hidden until the mouse moves; hosts show the cursor when they unlock). `GetElement()` for `element()`. |
| `dom/PointerLockOptions.h`, `.idl` | `port` | `DOM/Dicts/PointerLockOptions.hpp` (new) | on | |
| `dom/Element+PointerLock.idl`, `Element::requestPointerLock` | `port*` | `Element::RequestPointerLock()` | on | tested. Always takes the options (upstream gates them behind a setting); the promise is an optional callback. |
| `dom/Document+PointerLock.idl`, `Document::exitPointerLock` | `port` | `Document::ExitPointerLock()` | on | tested. No `onpointerlockchange` or `onpointerlockerror` (no scripting). |
| `dom/DocumentOrShadowRoot+PointerLock.idl`, `TreeScope::pointerLockElement` | `port*` | `DocumentOrShadowRoot::PointerLockElement()` | on | tested. Retargets as `ActiveElement()` does, for `ancestorElementInThisScope`. |
| `page/ChromeClient.h` (`requestPointerLock`, `requestPointerUnlock`, `hasAccessoryMousePointingDevice`) | `port` | `ChromeClient` | on | The defaults: unsupported, not unlocked, no mouse. |
| `platform/PlatformMouseEvent.h` (`unadjustedMovementDelta`) | `port*` | `PlatformMouseEvent::UnadjustedMovementDelta()` | on | A setter for the host. |
| `page/EventHandler.cpp` (the pointer lock parts) | `port*` | `EventHandler` | on | tested. Presses, moves, releases and the wheel go to the locked element; Escape unlocks. A locked press still notifies the window's activation first (upstream's gesture indicator is its host's, around the whole event). The force events (`webkitmouseforce*`) are dropped (non-standard); the context menu's check comes with `sendContextMenuEvent` (B7d). |
| The call sites: `Element::removedFromAncestor`, the document's detaching and back/forward cache state, `LocalDOMWindow::alert`, `confirm` and `prompt`, `PointerCaptureController::setPointerCapture` (step 3) | `port` | `ExtensibilityHooks`, `Document`, `LocalDOMWindow`, `PointerCaptureController` | on | tested (removal, capture). The FIXMEs went. |

**Bugs fixed:**
- Pointers captured before the pointer was locked kept their capture: upstream releases captures (`pointerLockWasApplied`) only when a held lock moves to another element, not when the host first applies it (its own FIXME says so). The standard releases them whenever a lock is applied; `DidAcquirePointerLock()` does too.

**Added (upstream API):** `PointerLockController`, `PointerLockOptions`, `PointerLockRequestResult`, `Element::RequestPointerLock()`, `Document::ExitPointerLock()`, `DocumentOrShadowRoot::PointerLockElement()`, the chrome client's `RequestPointerLock()`, `RequestPointerUnlock()` and `HasAccessoryMousePointingDevice()`, `PlatformMouseEvent::UnadjustedMovementDelta()`, `Page::GetPointerLockController()`, the `pointerlockchange` and `pointerlockerror` event names.
**Differences:** as in the table. A request needs the window's transient activation (Booey has no gesture indicator), so it may come from a timer up to five seconds after a press or a key, where upstream's must come while the input is being handled. Unadjusted movement is offered wherever the host has a mouse (upstream only on macOS and iOS); Krystal.PAL reports the device's raw movement on Windows.
**Host:** Krystal.PAL's window locks the pointer (`IWindow::SetPointerLocked()`): it keeps the cursor hidden in the client area, puts it back at the centre after each move, and reports the cursor's movement (with the system's acceleration) and raw input's (without it) as `OnLockedMouseMove` and `LockedMouseMoveEvent`; it unlocks on losing focus and puts the cursor back where it was. Krystal.UI's view answers the chrome client through a handler the host sets (`SetPointerLockHandler()`; without one, there's no pointer lock), fails while the window doesn't have focus, loses the lock when it does, hides the cursor while locked, and sends `LockedMouseMoved()` to the locked element where the mouse was. Its mouse moves now carry their movement (`movementX` and `movementY`) unlocked too. The editor wires the window to the page.
Tests: `tests/Page/PointerLockController.cpp`: 2 cases / 93 assertions; Krystal.UI's `View: pointer lock`: 1 case / 21 assertions pass.

## Pen and touch from the host (B7b, 2026-10-25)

Part B7b of pointer and touch input (*B7 plan* in `docs/booey/ROADMAP.md`): pens and touches come from Windows through Krystal.PAL and Krystal.UI's view, pens as the mouse's events with pointer type `pen`, touches as touch events and pointer events of type `touch`. Graph from `dom/TouchEvent.h` (headers-only): the new files are `Touch`, `TouchList`, `TouchEvent` and `platform/PlatformTouchEvent.h` and `PlatformTouchPoint.h`. Read in full: those, their IDL, `DocumentTouch` and `Document+Touch.idl`, `NavigatorMaxTouchPoints.idl`, `dom/glib/PointerEventGLib.cpp` (the touch constructors GTK and WPE build), the touch parts of `PointerEvent.h`, `page/PointerCaptureController` and `page/EventHandler` (`handleTouchEvent` and its helpers, `clear`, the mouse move hit type, `dispatchSyntheticTouchEventIfEnabled`), and `Navigator::maxTouchPoints`.

| WebKit | Verdict | Krystal | CMake | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `dom/Touch.h`, `.cpp`, `Touch.idl` | `port*` | `DOM/Touch.hpp`, `src/...` (new) | on | tested. The standard's names (`RadiusX()`, `RadiusY()`, `RotationAngle()`, `Force()`) for upstream's non-standard `webkitRadiusX` and the rest. No constructor, as upstream (the standard's `TouchInit` isn't ported). The frame scale factor is the frame view's. |
| `dom/TouchList.h`, `.cpp`, `TouchList.idl` | `port` | `DOM/TouchList.hpp`, `src/...` (new) | on | tested. |
| `dom/TouchEvent.h`, `.cpp`, `TouchEvent.idl` (with `TouchEventInit`) | `port*` | `DOM/TouchEvent.hpp`, `src/...`, `DOM/Dicts/TouchEventInit.hpp` (new) | on | tested. The dictionary is the standard's (`EventModifierInit` with lists of touches; upstream's is `UIEventInit` with touch lists). `Event::IsTouchEvent()`. |
| `dom/DocumentTouch.h`, `.cpp`, `Document+Touch.idl` | `drop` | | | `createTouch()` and `createTouchList()` were dropped from the standard. |
| `dom/NavigatorMaxTouchPoints.idl`, `page/Navigator.cpp` (`maxTouchPoints`) | `port*` | `Navigator::MaxTouchPoints()` | on | tested. The frame's media environment's `MaxTouchPoints` (new), which the host sets; upstream's is 0 off iOS. |
| `platform/PlatformTouchEvent.h`, `PlatformTouchPoint.h` | `port*` | `Platform/PlatformTouchEvent.hpp`, `PlatformTouchPoint.hpp` (new) | on | Public constructors and the coalesced and predicted events' setters, for the host (upstream's ports subclass them); `PlatformEvent`'s touch types. |
| `dom/glib/PointerEventGLib.cpp` (the touch constructors) | `port*` | `PointerEvent` | on | tested. Touches' pointer ids start at 3, after the pen's (upstream's GLib ones at 2). `PointerIdForTouch()` is new. |
| `page/PointerCaptureController.h`, `.cpp` (`dispatchEventForTouchAtIndex`, `dispatchOverOrOutEvent`, `dispatchEnterOrLeaveEvent`, the previous target) | `port*` | `PointerCaptureController` | on | tested. The FIXME went. `pointerenter` and `pointerleave` go to every element of the chain (FIXME, as the mouse's: targets can't say which listeners they have). |
| `page/EventHandler.cpp` (`handleTouchEvent`, `eventNameForTouchPointState`, `hitTestResultInFrame`, the touch members, `clear`, mouse moves while touching) | `port*` | `EventHandler::HandleTouchEvent()` | on | tested. Returns a `bool` (no remote frames). Every document gets touch events (`hasTouchEventHandlers` is a FIXME, for the same reason). Targets get their touch events in the order they were first seen (upstream's in a hash set's order). WPE's synthesised cancel and the inspector's hook are dropped. Touch event emulation from the mouse (`dispatchSyntheticTouchEventIfEnabled`, a developer setting) isn't ported. |
| `platform/PointerID.h` (the pen) | `port*` | `PenPointerID` (new) | on | The pen's pointer is 2. |

**Bugs fixed:**
- `touchcancel` was cancelable; the standard says it isn't.
- A touch's radius was multiplied by the zoom rather than divided by it, so it wasn't in CSS pixels as its position is.
- Pointer events for touches from devices that report no pressure had a pressure of 0 while down (the standard says 0.5), and a width and height of 0 from devices that report no contact size (the standard says 1).
- Pointer events for touches had the touch's position in the view as their screen position.
- GTK's path dispatched `pointercancel` without cancelling the pointer, so a cancelled touch kept its capture and its pointer's state; it goes through `cancelPointer()` now, as iOS's does (with `pointerout`, `pointerleave` and the capture's release).
- The pointers of ended touches were never forgotten off iOS (only iOS's UI process calls `touchWithIdentifierWasRemoved`), so a reused touch id kept the old touch's state; `HandleTouchEvent` forgets them once their events are dispatched.

**Added (upstream API):** `Touch`, `TouchList`, `TouchEvent` and its dictionary, `PlatformTouchEvent`, `PlatformTouchPoint`, `EventHandler::HandleTouchEvent()`, `PointerCaptureController::DispatchEventForTouchAtIndex()`, `PointerEvent`'s touch constructors, `Navigator::MaxTouchPoints()`, the touch event names.
**Differences:** as in the table. A pen comes as the mouse's events (`PlatformMouseEvent` with pointer type `pen` and id 2), as upstream's GTK and macOS pens do, and its tilt and twist reach its pointer events through `PenOrientation` on `PlatformMouseEvent` and `MouseEvent` (new; upstream's only pens with tilt, iOS's, come as touches). The pen's eraser is the eraser button (5, `buttons` 32) and its barrel button the right button, as the standard's table has them. A stationary touch has a `pointermove` with every change to the others, as upstream's GLib path. No `ontouch*` handlers (no scripting).
**Host:** Krystal.PAL takes pens and touches from Windows' pointer messages (`WM_POINTERENTER`, `WM_POINTERDOWN`, `WM_POINTERUPDATE`, `WM_POINTERUP`, `WM_POINTERLEAVE`; `WM_POINTERCAPTURECHANGED` cancels): `PointerInput` (id, position, contact, primary, pressure, tilt, twist, contact size, barrel button, eraser), the window callback `OnPointer` and its event `PointerInputEvent`; the system's press and hold and flicks are turned off. Without the callback, the system turns them into mouse input as before. `pal::GetPointingDevices()` reports the mouse, pens, touch screens and their touches. Krystal.UI's view has `PenInput()` (the mouse's path, with click counting), `TouchInput()` (touch ids from the lowest free, every touch on the screen in each event) and `SetPointingDevices()` (the pointer and hover media features and `maxTouchPoints`); the editor sends the window's pens and touches to the page and tells it the devices.
Tests: `tests/Page/PenAndTouch.cpp`: 4 cases / 96 assertions; Krystal.UI's `View: pens and touches`: 1 case / 18 assertions pass.

## Backing sharing layers held weakly (B6d, 2026-10-25)

A bug found by B6d's sample (the editor's page with a fixed, animated reading bar): tearing the page down crashed in `RenderLayerBacking::ClearBackingSharingLayers`. A composited layer's backing keeps the layers that paint into it; upstream holds them weakly (`InlineWeakKeyListHashSet<RenderLayer>`), but Booey held raw pointers, so a sharing layer destroyed before its provider (as the render tree is torn down) left a dangling pointer the provider then followed.

| WebKit | Verdict | Krystal | CMake | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rendering/RenderLayerBacking.h`, `.cpp` (`m_backingSharingLayers` and its users) | `port` | `RenderLayerBacking` | on | tested by Krystal.UI's editor page cases. A list of `WeakPtr`s (Krystal.Core has no weak hash set; the lists are short), skipping destroyed layers as upstream's `dereferenceView` does; the compositor still hands over a `ListHashSet<RenderLayer *>` of live layers. |

**Bugs fixed:** the backing's sharing layers were raw pointers, so destroying a sharing layer before its provider crashed the provider's teardown (any page whose fixed or otherwise composited element had layers sharing its backing).
**Differences:** as in the table.
Tests: Krystal.UI's *View: the editor page's observers* and *View: the editor page's animations* crashed without the fix.

## The Web Animations interfaces from C++ (B6b, 2026-10-25)

Part B6b of the Web Animations API (*B6 plan* in `docs/booey/ROADMAP.md`): what scripts do with animations, from C++. Effects get the timing interface and keyframes from C++ (both of the specification's forms, decision 1), animations get the `bindings*` members, the ready and finished promises (`AnimationPromise`, decision 2) and `commitStyles()`, CSS animations stop following the properties C++ overrides, and elements, documents and shadow roots get `animate()` and `getAnimations()`. No new upstream `.cpp` files: the bindings halves of files already ported (G9), the dictionaries as structs, and `Element`'s, `Document`'s and `ShadowRoot`'s animation members.

| `animation/AnimationEffect.h`, `.cpp` (`getBindingsTiming`, `getBindingsComputedTiming`, `bindingsUpdateTiming`, `updateTiming`, the `ExceptionOr` setters) | `port` | `AnimationEffect` | on | tested. Were FIXMEs; `SetIterationStart` and `SetIterations` return a `TypeError` instead of a flag, and `SetIterationStart` returns early on an unchanged value, as upstream. |

## Content visibility (B5d, 2026-10-24)

Step B5d of observers (*B5 plan* in `docs/booey/ROADMAP.md`): an element with `content-visibility: auto` is relevant to the user while it's near the viewport (an intersection observer per document, rooted at the document), focused, selected or holding an element in the top layer, and skips its contents otherwise; the relevancy is checked in the rendering update's new content relevancy step, first in the resize observations step (the initial determination), and `contentvisibilityautostatechange` fires when it changes. Layout now skips the contents of `content-visibility: hidden` and of skipped `auto` elements (painting and hit testing already did), lays them out when their geometry is asked for, and scrolling to skipped content makes it relevant first. Graph from `dom/ContentVisibilityDocumentState.h` (headers-only, following `css/`, `style/`, `page/`, `html/`, `dom/` and `rendering/`): 142 files, all ported except `dom/ContentVisibilityDocumentState` and `dom/ContentVisibilityAutoStateChangeEvent` themselves. The used content visibility, `IsSkippedContent`, `IsSkippedContentRoot` and the skipped painting were ported with the render tree.

|---|---|---|---|---|

The callback is a function (`IntersectionObserverCallback` is a `Func`); the viewport proximities are keyed by the element's address (no weak hash map; an element's entry goes when it's unobserved, which its renderer's destruction does); no obscured insets (no `contentInsetBackgroundFillEnabled` setting). |
