**Bugs fixed:** none (new code).
**Added (upstream API):** listed in the table; `ImageDecoder::AccessibilityDescription`, which upstream's decoders have and Booey's lacked.
**Differences:**
- Decoding is synchronous: there's no decoding work queue, so asynchronous decoding (`DecodingMode::Asynchronous`, `decode()`) decodes at once, and `Decode`'s callbacks are called before it returns.
- No frame animator until G7d: the current frame is the primary frame, and nothing starts animations.
- No colour spaces or HDR: images are sRGB, and the colour space, headroom, HDR gain map and `ShouldDecodeToHDR` paths are dropped; no subsampling (as upstream outside Core Graphics).
- `currentPreTransformedNativeImage` applies the orientation to the pixels itself, where upstream draws into an image buffer: Booey's image buffers record display lists, not pixels. A density-corrected size isn't applied (FIXME).
- Image buffers still don't draw as native images (`nativeImageForDrawing`, FIXME): drawing backends render their display lists.
- No image adapter, no asynchronous animation start, no `allowsAnimation` override or system animation controls; `Image::create(observer)` and `supportsType` wait for G7b.

Tests: `tests/Platform/ImageDecoders/ScalableImageDecoder.cpp` (new): 8 cases (sniffing; PNG, premultiplied or not, in parts and truncated; JPEG and its orientation; WebP; GIF; BMP; ICO); `tests/Graphics/BitmapImage.cpp` (new): 7 cases (metadata, empty images and data that isn't an image, orientation, the recorded draws and patterns, a single pixel drawing as its colour, the observer, `Decode`, images made from native images); the images are generated with Pillow into `include/Krystal.Booey.Tests/Platform/ImageDecoders/TestImages.hpp`. The whole suite passes (2312 cases; 7 expected failures).


## Loading and CSS images (G7b, 2026-10-20)

Part G7b of the graphics redesign (*G7 plan* in `docs/gfx/DESIGN.md`): `url()` images load through the host and paint. Graphs (headers-only, following `css/`, `style/`, `loader/` and `platform/network/`): `loader/cache/CachedResourceLoader.h` 94 files, `loader/cache/CachedImage.h` 58, nearly all the network stack (frame loaders, document loaders, subresource loaders, HTTP, security origins, content security policy, resource timing) that the trimmed port leaves out. The host seam is upstream's own: a `LoaderStrategy` (the platform strategy WebKit's embedders implement), here loading a URL and calling back with the whole response.

| WebKit | Verdict | Krystal | CMake | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `loader/LoaderStrategy.h`, `platform/PlatformStrategies.h` | `port*` | `Loader/LoaderStrategy.hpp`, `Platform/PlatformStrategies.hpp`, `src/...` | on | tested. `LoadResource(frame, request, options, completion)`: the host calls back once with a `LoadedResource` (response and bytes) or a `ResourceError`, at any time; Booey queues the completion as a networking task. No subresource loaders, streaming, redirects, cancellation, pings or preconnects. The host sets the strategy (`PlatformStrategies::SetLoaderStrategy`); without one, loads fail. |
| `platform/network/ResourceRequest.h`, `ResourceResponse.h`, `ResourceError.h` | `port*` | `Platform/Network/ResourceRequest.hpp`, `ResourceResponse.hpp`, `ResourceError.hpp` | on | tested. The URL; the URL, MIME type, expected length and text encoding; the domain, code, failing URL, description and type. No HTTP. |
| `platform/network/DataURLDecoder.h`, `.cpp` | `port*` | `Platform/Network/DataURLDecoder.hpp`, `src/...` | on | tested. Synchronous `decode` only; the media type is parsed simply (FIXME: `ParsedContentType`). `data:` URLs are decoded by Booey, never the host. |
| `wtf/text/Base64.h`, `.cpp` (`base64Decode`) | `port*` | Krystal.Core `Text/Base64.hpp`, `src/Text/Base64.cpp` | on | tested (Krystal.Core). Decoding only, with `ValidatePadding` and `IgnoreWhitespace`. |
| `loader/FetchOptions.h`, `loader/ResourceLoaderOptions.h`, `platform/ReferrerPolicy.h` | `port*` | `Loader/FetchOptions.hpp`, `Loader/ResourceLoaderOptions.hpp` | on | The mode, credentials, referrer policy and integrity; the callback, buffering, caching and content security policy policies and the opaque source flag. Members are named after what they hold (`RequestMode`, `Caching`, ...), not their types. |
| `loader/cache/CachedResource.h`, `.cpp` | `port*` | `Loader/Cache/CachedResource.hpp`, `src/...` | on | tested. Clients (counted), status, sizes, loading and `whenLoaded`, `finish`, the response and error, the decoded data deletion timer; `load` asks the strategy (or decodes a `data:` URL) and finishes as upstream's subresource loader would. Reference counted (see the differences). No revalidation, preloads, CORS, priorities or digests. |
| `loader/cache/CachedResourceClient.h`, `CachedImageClient.h`, `CachedResourceClientWalker.h`, `CachedResourceHandle.h` | `port*` | `Loader/Cache/...` | on | tested. The handle holds a reference. |
| `loader/cache/CachedResourceRequest.h` | `port*` | `Loader/Cache/CachedResourceRequest.hpp` | on | The request, options and initiator type. |
| `loader/cache/CachedImage.h`, `.cpp` | `port*` | `Loader/Cache/CachedImage.hpp`, `src/...` | on | tested. The image made from the data (a `BitmapImage` observed through `CachedImageObserver`), its sizes for renderers, the clients' notifications, decoding errors. FIXME: SVG images, the broken image (G7c), the streamed data back-off, asynchronous decoding's waiting clients. |
| `loader/cache/MemoryCache.h`, `.cpp` | `port*` | `Loader/Cache/MemoryCache.hpp`, `src/...` | on | tested. Resources by URL, live and dead sizes, capacities, pruning dead then live resources, eviction, disabling. One least recently used list (no size-adjusted lists or live decoded list); no sessions, partitions or origins. |
| `loader/cache/CachedResourceLoader.h`, `.cpp` | `port*` | `Loader/Cache/CachedResourceLoader.hpp`, `src/...` | on | tested. `requestImage` (the memory cache, the revalidation policy without HTTP, immediate failures), the document's resources and their collection, image loading switches. Other resource types, request counting and security checks are FIXMEs. |
| `css/values/primitives/CSSURLModifiers.cpp` (`applyModifiersToLoaderOptions`) | `port` | `src/CSS/Values/Primitives/URLModifiers.cpp` | on | Was a FIXME. |
| `css/CSSImageValue.cpp` (loading) | `port` | `src/CSS/Values/ImageValue.cpp` | on | tested. `isPending`, `loadImage`, `cachedImage`, `knownToBeOpaque`, `customTraverseSubresources`, and the cached image shared with copies. |
| `rendering/style/StyleImage.h` (`load`, clients) and every subclass | `port*` | `Rendering/Style/...` | on | tested. `StyleCachedImage` in full but SVG resources; `StyleMultiImage` selects and forwards; generated images count their clients; crossfade and filter images load their inputs (FIXME: following them as clients). |
| `style/StylePendingResources.h`, `.cpp` | `port*` | `Style/PendingResources.hpp`, `src/...` | on | tested. FIXME: user agent shadow trees and the anonymous mode for masks. |
| `RenderObject`'s cached image client emulation (`CachedImageListener`), `RenderElement`'s image registration (`updateFillImages`, `updateImage`, `updateShapeImage`, `willBeDestroyed`) and `loadPendingResources` calls, `imageChanged` in `RenderBox`, `RenderInline`, `RenderListMarker`, `RenderTableCol`, `RenderTableRow`, `RenderTableSection` | `port*` | `src/Rendering/...` | on | tested. `RenderObject::Repaint` schedules a rendering update (no repaint rects). List markers size themselves by their images. |
| `rendering/style/StyleImageSet.cpp` (supported types), `style/values/shapes/StyleShapeOutside.cpp` (`isValid`), `style/values/backgrounds/StyleFillLayers.h` (`imagesAreLoaded`) | `port` | `src/...` | on | Were FIXMEs. |

**Bugs fixed:** none.
**Added (upstream API):** listed in the table; `Document::GetCachedResourceLoader`, `RenderElement::GetImageOrientation`.
**Differences:**
- Cached resources are reference counted: handles and the memory cache hold references, and a resource dies with the last, where upstream deletes it by hand once it has no clients, handles or loader and is out of the cache. Clients still remove themselves before they're destroyed.
- The memory cache counts a resource's encoded and decoded bytes, not its overhead, which changes as the response arrives (upstream's totals drift by it).
- Loads complete whole: no partial data, so images decode once all their data is there.
- Without a page, a frame still loads; documents without a frame don't.
- A load repaints by scheduling a rendering update (any change repaints the whole page).

Tests: `tests/Loader/Cache/CachedResourceLoader.cpp` (new): 8 cases (loading as style is set and painting once loaded, the memory cache shared, failed loads and data that isn't an image, `data:` URLs, no strategy, the rendering update, pruning, list markers); `tests/Platform/Network/DataURLDecoder.cpp` (new): 2 cases; Krystal.Core `tests/Text/Base64.cpp` (new): 3 cases. The whole suite passes (2322 cases; 7 expected failures).

## Images in HTML (G7c, 2026-10-20)

Part G7c of the graphics redesign (*G7 plan* in `docs/gfx/DESIGN.md`): `<img>` loads its selected source, fires `load` and `error`, and paints, with `<picture>` and `<source>`; `content: url()` images render. Graphs (headers-only, following `css/`, `style/`, `html/`, `loader/` and `rendering/`): `loader/ImageLoader.h` 61 files, `rendering/RenderImage.h` 112, `html/HTMLImageElement.h` 96; beyond what G7b brought, mostly form association, image maps, lazy loading (intersection observers), promises, archives and accessibility, which stay out. Booey's `HTMLImageElement`, `HTMLPictureElement` and `HTMLSourceElement` are written from the HTML standard (their attribute reflection stays); upstream's behaviour joins them through Booey's DOM hooks (`OnAttributeChanged`, `OnInsert`, `OnRemove`, `OnMove`, `OnAdopt`) in place of upstream's `attributeChanged`, `insertedIntoAncestor`, `removedFromAncestor` and `didMoveToNewDocument`.

**Bugs fixed:**
- `HTMLElement::IsHTMLPictureElement` tested for `HTMLElementInterface::Pre`, so no `<picture>` was one (and every `<pre>` was).
**Added (upstream API):** listed in the table; `RenderObject::IsRenderImage`, `RenderElement::HasShapeOutside`, `RenderElement::IsContentDataSupported`, `Element::ImageSourceURL`, `Element::DidAttachRenderers`; node cast traits for `HTMLImageElement`, `HTMLPictureElement` and `HTMLSourceElement`.
**Differences:**
- The before-load step (upstream's leftover `beforeload` handling) runs as the image changes: the renderer takes the new image at once when the element is connected and the document has a render tree.
- Images load only while the document has a render tree, as upstream; a document parsed before it has a frame loads none until its images change or move (the view parses in its frame, as a navigation does).
- A `<source>` decides whether its insertion is a relevant mutation by whether its parent `<picture>` changed, since Booey's insertion hook doesn't say which node was inserted.
- The `width` and `height` getters return the reflected values only when the element has no renderer; with one, its content box (as upstream).
- A load repaints by scheduling a rendering update (any change repaints the whole page).

Tests: `tests/HTML/HTMLImageElement.cpp` (new): 7 cases (loading, `load` and painting; `error`, alt text and collapsing; attribute sizes and object-fit; `srcset` densities, widths and `sizes`; `<picture>` sources by type and media, with a source's sizes, and removing one; changing the source; generated content images); `tests/HTML/Parser/HTMLSrcsetParser.cpp` (new): 2 cases; `tests/CSS/Parser/SizesAttributeParser.cpp` (new): 3 cases; `tests/HTML/MicroParsers/Numbers.cpp`: 1 new case; the G7b test loader moved to `Krystal.Booey.Tests/Loader/TestLoader.hpp`. The whole suite passes (2335 cases; 7 expected failures).

## Animated images (G7d, 2026-10-20)

Part G7d of the graphics redesign (*G7 plan* in `docs/gfx/DESIGN.md`): GIF, APNG and animated WebP images animate, in `<img>` and CSS, and pause while they can't be seen. Graph (headers-only, following `platform/graphics/`): `platform/graphics/ImageFrameAnimator.h` 9 files, all ported in G7a but the work queue (`ImageFrameWorkQueue`), which stays out. The G7a decoders already read the frames, their durations and the loop counts (now tested).

| WebKit | Verdict | Krystal | CMake | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `platform/graphics/ImageFrameAnimator.h`, `.cpp` | `port*` | `Graphics/ImageFrameAnimator.hpp`, `src/...` | on | tested. On Booey's timers, in the host's time (`ThreadTimers::CurrentTime`); the animator holds its source by reference (the source owns it). FIXME: requesting the next frame's decode ahead (no work queue). |
| `platform/graphics/BitmapImageSource.h`, `.cpp` (animation) | `port*` | `Graphics/BitmapImageSource.hpp`, `src/...` | on | tested. `frameAnimator`, `startAnimation`, `stopAnimation`, `resetAnimation`, `isAnimating`, `hasEverAnimated`, `isAnimationAllowed`, `currentFrameIndex`, `imageFrameAtIndexAvailable`, `isPendingDecodingAtIndex` (never: decoding is synchronous), `decode` with an animator, `currentNativeImageForDrawing` starting the animation, the animator in the dump. |
| `rendering/RenderElement.h`, `.cpp` (`isVisibleIgnoringGeometry`, `isVisibleInDocumentRect`, `isVisibleInViewport`, `imageFrameAvailable`, `imageVisibleInViewport`, `didRemoveCachedImageClient`, `repaintForPausedImageAnimationsIfNeeded`, `allowsAnimation`, the paused flag and its clean-up in `willBeDestroyed`) | `port*` | `src/Rendering/RenderElement.cpp` | on | tested. See the differences for the rect. FIXME: suspended documents, off-screen views, animation controls (`allowsAnimation` is always true), SVG images. |
| `rendering/RenderView.h`, `.cpp` (`addRendererWithPausedImageAnimations`, `removeRendererWithPausedImageAnimations`, `resumePausedImageAnimationsIfNeeded`) | `port*` | `src/Rendering/RenderView.cpp` | on | tested. Raw pointers (renderers remove themselves when destroyed, images when their client goes). FIXME: SVG elements. |
| `page/LocalFrameView.cpp` (`viewportContentsChanged`, `resumeVisibleImageAnimations`, their calls from `setFrameRect`, `scrollPositionChanged` and the post-layout tasks), `rendering/RenderLayerScrollableArea.cpp` (the call after a scroll) | `port*` | `src/Page/LocalFrameView.cpp`, `src/Page/LocalFrameViewLayoutContext.cpp`, `src/Rendering/RenderLayerScrollableArea.cpp` | on | tested. Only the image animations; intersection observers, lazy loading, content visibility, throttling and subframes are FIXMEs. |

**Bugs fixed:** none.
**Added (upstream API):** listed in the table.
**Differences:**
- Without repaint rects, a renderer is visible when its absolute visual overflow (or bounding box) meets the visible content, unclipped by its ancestors (upstream's `absoluteClippedOverflowRectForRepaint`): an image clipped out by a scrolling box that's itself in view keeps animating.
- The current frame decodes before the animation starts, so its duration (known once it's decoded) times it; upstream starts first and decodes the next frame ahead on its work queue.
- A frame's timer starts when the frame is drawn, as upstream; nothing redraws a frame that isn't painted, so an animation also waits while its page isn't painted.

Tests: `tests/Platform/ImageDecoders/ScalableImageDecoder.cpp`: 1 new case (GIF, APNG and WebP frames, durations and loop counts); `tests/Graphics/BitmapImage.cpp`: 2 new cases (frames advancing in the host's time, late frames, resetting; stopping after the loops); `tests/HTML/HTMLImageElement.cpp`: 2 new cases (an `<img>` and a CSS background animating as they're painted; pausing out of view and resuming); the animated images in `Krystal.Booey.Tests/Platform/ImageDecoders/AnimatedImages.hpp` (new, made with Pillow). The whole suite passes (2340 cases; 7 expected failures).

## Style sheets (G8a, 2026-10-20)

Part G8a of the graphics redesign (*G8 plan* in `docs/gfx/DESIGN.md`): `<link rel=stylesheet>` and `@import` load through G7b's loader and the host's `LoaderStrategy`. Graphs (headers-only, following `css/`, `style/`, `html/` and `loader/`): `loader/cache/CachedCSSStyleSheet.h` 31 files, `html/HTMLLinkElement.h` 88; beyond G7b, the link loader (preloads, icons, manifests), subresource integrity, the text resource decoder's encodings and the frame loader, which stay out. Most of the rest was already here: the style scope's pending sheets and active sheet collection, the tree resolver holding back styles while head sheets load, `StyleSheetContents::CheckLoaded` and the owners' notifications (ported with style resolution). Booey's `HTMLLinkElement` is written from the HTML standard; upstream's behaviour joins it through Booey's DOM hooks, as `<img>`'s did in G7c.

**Bugs fixed:** none.
**Added (upstream API):** listed in the table; node cast traits for `HTMLLinkElement`; `HTMLLinkElement::IsDisabled`, `IsEnabledViaScript`, `StyleSheetIsLoading`.
**Differences:**
- Sheets decode as UTF-8 only.
- A `<link>` is "created by the parser" (implicitly render-blocking) if it's inserted before the parser finishes it, as `<style>`'s owner decides; upstream passes the flag to the constructor.
- The subresource cache policy is the host's per document: it doesn't go back to `Verify` once the document has loaded, but the validated URLs keep a document from loading a URL twice.
- Holding back rendering is the tree resolver's (no styles, so no renderers, while head sheets load); Booey's render-blocking list (`RenderBlocking`) is kept up to date but nothing reads it yet.

Tests: `tests/HTML/HTMLLinkElement.cpp`: 5 new cases (loading and holding back rendering; nested and media imports; import cycles; failures and types that aren't CSS; media, disabled sheets, links added and removed); `tests/Loader/Cache/CachedResourceLoader.cpp`: 1 new case (cache policies); the parse-in-a-frame fixture and the load event counter moved to `Krystal.Booey.Tests/Loader/PageInFrameFixture.hpp`, and the test loader serves text with a type. The whole suite passes (2346 cases; 7 expected failures).

**Bugs fixed:**
- Krystal.Core's `text::Decode` looked for a byte order mark by comparing the whole input with it, so it only found one in an input that was nothing else; it now checks the input's start. Style sheets with a byte order mark (as the repository's files have) began with a stray U+FEFF that swallowed their first rule: the editor's `@import` of `widgets.css` (and its `html` rule) never applied (G8a; found by rendering the editor page).
**Added (upstream API):** listed in the table; `Document::FontSelectorIfExists`; `CSSFontSelector::GetDocument`, `GetCSSFontFaceSet` and `FontFaceClient`.
**Differences:**
- The custom platform data copies the font file's bytes (a FreeType face owns its memory), so nothing wraps the cached resource.
- `CSSFontFaceClient` is abstractly ref-counted and weak-pointable as upstream, but the selector's client is a member object (`FontFaceClientImpl`) that forwards its count; `CSSFontFaceSet` calls its selector's `FontModified` instead of keeping observers.
- No settings for font loading: timings follow `font-display`, completions are never ignored, and installed fonts are always allowed.
Tests: `tests/CSS/Font/FontFace.cpp` (6 cases: loading once text uses a font, in each format, sources in order, matching by weight, style and `unicode-range`, `font-display` periods, faces following their rules), `tests/Loader/Cache/CachedFont.cpp` (2), `tests/Graphics/WOFFFileFormat.cpp` (2), `tests/HTML/HTMLLinkElement.cpp` (1 new: a sheet's byte order mark); the test fonts made from Ahem (WOFF, WOFF 2, CFF OpenType) are in `Krystal.Booey.Tests/data/webfonts/`, apart from the fonts tests register, and the test loader serves files (`AddFile`). The whole suite passes (2357 cases; 7 expected failures).

## The animation model and transitions (G9b, 2026-10-20)

**Bugs fixed:**
- `WebAnimation::updatePlaybackRate` divides the unconstrained current time by a zero pending playback rate when a finished animation's rate is set to zero; the spec says the start time is then the timeline time, which Krystal does.
**Added (upstream API):** listed in the table; event names `animationcancel`, `transitionrun`, `transitionstart`, `transitioncancel`, `cancel`, `finish` and `remove`; the `InternalAsyncTask` task source.
**Differences:**
- No promises, bindings or script-facing setters; the Web Animations interfaces wait for scripting.
- Time is the host's: the timelines controller's live time is `html::EventLoop::Current().Now()`, and the frozen time of an update is the page's rendering update timestamp. A document without a frame has no current time (upstream: no window).
- Without frame rate alignment or accelerated animations, `DocumentTimeline::ScheduleNextTick` assumes 15 ms frames (`FullSpeedAnimationInterval`).
- As upstream, a transition that finishes naturally leaves the running transitions first, so it isn't recorded as completed (`TransitionDidComplete` only keeps transitions still running).
Tests: `tests/Animation/AnimationEffectTiming.cpp` (3 cases: computed properties, phases, progress with fill modes, iterations, directions and timing functions), `tests/Animation/WebAnimation.cpp` (4: the document timeline, playing with pausing, rates, seeking and reversing, finishing and canceling with their events, effect stacks), `tests/Animation/CSSTransition.cpp` (8: starting and running, events, delays, reversing and replacing, canceling, which changes start transitions, `@starting-style`, removing the element). The whole suite passes (2382 cases; 7 expected failures).

**Bugs fixed:** none.
**Added (upstream API):** listed in the table.
**Differences:**
- As upstream, an element's animations created by markup are kept from the end of `animation-name` to its start (they're matched from the end); composite order comes from the `animation` list, not the collection.
- The pending animations get their start time from the last time the timelines controller cached, not from the cache itself (`_lastCachedCurrentTime`): the host runs the event loop once per frame, timers before tasks, so at 60 Hz the cache's 15 ms clearance timer always fired before the task processing the pending animations, and animations stayed pending forever (found in the editor: a frozen spinner). Krystal.UI's "View: animations run on the host's frames" covers it.
- An animation is created in the rendering update that resolves its style and starts at once (its phase is active while it's pending, with a hold time of zero), so its `animationstart` fires in that update.
Tests: `tests/Animation/CSSAnimation.cpp` (7 cases: an animation from `@keyframes`, its events, timing properties (iterations, direction, infinite, delay with backwards fill, forwards fill, `steps()`, a keyframe's timing function, implicit keyframes), the play state, changing `animation-name` (to another name, adding one, `none`, `display: none`), `@keyframes` rules added and changed, transitions and animations in composite order); the transition tests moved onto `include/Krystal.Booey.Tests/Animation/AnimationTestUtils.hpp`. The whole suite passes (2389 cases; 7 expected failures). Krystal.UI's `animations` page golden (paused animations at negative delays) matches Chrome's (largest difference 21, no pixel over the tolerance).

## Repainting only what changed (G10b to G10d, 2026-10-20)

Parts G10b to G10d of the graphics redesign (*G10 plan* in `docs/gfx/DESIGN.md`; the measurements are in *G10 as built*). G10b: the frame view collects damage and Krystal.UI's `View` keeps the painted page in a texture, repainting it only when it's damaged. G10c: upstream's repaint invalidation, so changes damage their own rects, and the view repaints only the damage. No `::backdrop` (FIXME: the top layer). |
| `page/LocalFrameViewLayoutContext.cpp` (the repaint region accumulator, the full repaint after the first layout) | `port` | `src/Page/LocalFrameViewLayoutContext.cpp` | on | Replaces G10b's whole-view repaint after each layout. |

**Bugs fixed:** none.
**Added (upstream API):** listed in the table.
**Differences:**
- Damage is collected in the frame view as a region, in the view's coordinates, and the host takes it once a frame; upstream tells the host window at once.
- Krystal.UI's `View::Paint` groups the damaged rects (merging two when their bounds waste no more than their own area, or while there are more than 8), records each group (`LocalFrameView::Paint` with that dirty rect), replays them under clips into a second texture, cleared, and copies those rects into the page texture (`BlitTexture`), so what was there is replaced rather than drawn over. The whole page is painted straight into the page texture.
- G10d, in Krystal.UI: corners within a sixteenth of a pixel of circular are drawn as circles (`ToCircularRoundedRect`): pixel snapping scales a box's radii with it, so circular corners came out a little elliptical and every rounded box was filled, shadowed and clipped through path masks.
Tests: Krystal.UI's `tests/Repaint.cpp` ("repainting only the damage leaves no stale pixels": a page through colour, hover, size, text, transform, opacity, position, `display` and `visibility` changes, inserted and removed content, scrolling a box and the page, and a transition, each frame compared with the whole page painted again; "damage is the rect that changed": a colour change, hover and a transform damage the box's rects) and `tests/View.cpp` ("damage", "an animation damages the page each frame"). The whole Booey suite passes (2389 cases; 7 expected failures); Krystal.UI's 48 cases pass in Debug and Release, goldens included.

Part G10e of the graphics redesign (*G10 as built* in `docs/gfx/DESIGN.md`): scrolling the view moved nothing and repainted all of it, so each frame of a scroll was a full repaint (about 97 ms in Debug on the editor page) and animations hitched. **Bugs fixed:**
- `RenderElement::AdjustStyleDifference` turned every `RepaintLayer` into `Repaint`, as if renderers had no layers (they have since G4c1), so a change that repaints a layer repainted only its renderer.
**Added (upstream API):** listed in the table.
**Differences:**
- Filters draw only through the graphics context: Booey has no software filters (`FilterRenderingMode::Software`, the appliers and filter images), so a filter that needs them (an uneven blur, `luminanceToAlpha`, reference filters) paints without its filter.
- A graphics style's blur radius is the CSS blur radius (twice the standard deviation), as shadows have it, not a box blur's kernel size.
- Krystal.UI's `GraphicsContextRender2D::BeginTransparencyLayer` maps the context's style to a Render2D layer filter (colour matrices as they are; blurs and shadow offsets through the current transform) and clears the style for what's drawn inside.
- Layers with filters aren't repaint containers (upstream's `containerForRepaint` checks `hasSoftwareFilters`, which is never set). Instead, a repaint inside a layer whose filter moves pixels grows to all the filter paints (`RenderLayer::AbsoluteFilterRepaintRect`), as Render2D can only blur what's inside the clip. Such a layer's repaint rects include it, so moving or resizing the layer repaints its old and new halo, and changing the filter repaints what it painted before and after (`RenderLayerModelObject`).
- The paint fixture in the tests can put the document in a page: filters paint only in a page (`Page::PreferredFilterRenderingModes`).
- **Known issue:** damage from outside a filter that moves pixels and covers only part of it (an animated image or a hover shadow beside a blurred box) paints the filter from clipped contents, leaving stale pixels (flicker in the editor's filter card). Compositing, where a filtered layer has its own backing and is filtered whole as it's composited, is the fix (planned next).
Tests: `tests/Rendering/CSSFilterRenderer.cpp` (effects per function, the styles, outsets, the display list a filtered layer paints, identity filters): 5 cases / 52 assertions pass. Krystal.UI's `tests/Golden.cpp` ("filters": colour matrices, component transfers, opacity, blurs, drop shadows, chains, a filtered group with an overflowing child and a filter inside opacity, against Chrome: mean difference 0.48, 69 of 86,400 pixels over the tolerance) and `tests/Repaint.cpp` ("changes inside filters leave no stale pixels": changes inside a blur, moving and changing shadows, adding and removing filters and a filter transition). Render2D's layer filters are in Krystal.Gfx's "Golden: layer filters" (mean difference 0.33 against Chrome). The whole Booey suite passes (2394 cases; 7 expected failures); Krystal.UI's 51 cases and Krystal.Gfx's 125 pass.

## The compositor (G12b, 2026-10-21)

Part G12b of compositing (*G12 plan* in `docs/gfx/DESIGN.md`): the compositor decides which layers get backings of their own, builds the graphics layer tree from them (G12a) and sends repaints to the backing they hit; Krystal.UI's `View` composites that tree (*G12b as built*). Graph from `rendering/RenderLayerCompositor.cpp` (headers-only): 284 files, nearly all ported already; the new ones are below. Graph from `rendering/RenderLayerBacking.cpp`: nothing new beyond these.

| WebKit | Verdict | Krystal | CMake | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rendering/RenderLayerCompositor.h`, `.cpp` | `port*` | `Rendering/RenderLayerCompositor.hpp`, `src/...` | on | tested. Compositing is on when the host gives the page a graphics layer factory (`ChromeClient::GetGraphicsLayerFactory`); then it's forced, as upstream's accelerated compositing mode, with the scroll layers upstream's viewless ports use (overflow controls host > frame clipping > frame scrolled contents > content root). All compositing triggers are allowed and the policy is always normal. Fixed position compositing is off (as the setting, until G12d); animations never composite (G12c). No scrolling coordinator, sticky or anchor positioned layers, page scale, obscured insets, rubber banding, iframes or widgets, canvas, video or plug-ins, event regions, tiled backings or layer flush throttling (FIXMEs). |
| `rendering/RenderLayerBacking.h`, `.cpp` | `port*` | `Rendering/RenderLayerBacking.hpp`, `src/...` | on | tested. No scrolling nodes, tiled backings, event and interaction regions, video, canvas, models or separated layers (FIXMEs). |
| `rendering/RenderGeometryMap.h`, `.cpp`, `RenderGeometryMapStep` | `port*` | `Rendering/RenderGeometryMap.hpp`, `src/...` | on | tested through the compositor. No fragmented flows or SVG roots; no debug check against the renderers' own mapping. `PushMappingToContainer` on `RenderElement`, `RenderBox`, `RenderInline` and `RenderView`; `PushOntoGeometryMap` on `RenderElement`. |
| `rendering/LayerOverlapMap.h`, `.cpp` | `port` | `Rendering/LayerOverlapMap.hpp`, `src/...` | on | tested. Raw layer pointers rather than `CheckedRef`. |
| `rendering/LayerAncestorClippingStack.h`, `.cpp` | `port*` | `Rendering/LayerAncestorClippingStack.hpp`, `src/...` | on | No scrolling coordinator proxy nodes. |
| `page/ChromeClient.h` (`attachRootGraphicsLayer`, `graphicsLayerFactory`) | `adapt` | `Page/ChromeClient.hpp` | on | Only the compositing hooks; `Page` owns one (`EmptyChromeClient` by default). |
| `page/LayoutOptions` (`LayoutOptions::UpdateCompositingLayers`) | `port*` | `DOM/Enums/LayoutOptions.hpp` | on | Only the compositing option. |
| `rendering/RenderLayer.h`, `.cpp` (compositing) | `port` | `Rendering/RenderLayer.hpp`, `src/...` | on | The compositing dirty bits, indirect compositing reasons, backings and backing sharing, the enclosing compositing layer, overlap bounds, painted content queries, the backdrop root and the scrolling scopes; the compositing FIXMEs are gone. |
| `rendering/RenderObject.cpp`, `RenderView.cpp`, `RenderBoxModelObject.cpp`, `RenderLayerModelObject.cpp` (compositing) | `port` | | on | Repaint containers are the enclosing compositing layers, repaints go to their backings; `RenderView::Compositor()`, `ContentChanged`. |
| `page/LocalFrameView.cpp`, `LocalFrameViewLayoutContext.cpp`, `dom/Document.cpp`, `page/Page.cpp` (compositing) | `port` | | on | Flushing compositing state, entering compositing mode, the scrollbar and scroll corner layers, compositing updates after style changes and layout, `Page::FinalizeRenderingUpdate` (no drawing area: it flushes compositing state). |

**Bugs fixed:**
- `RenderLayerBacking::updateAncestorClippingStack` moves the clip data into the backing's stack and then passes the moved-from list to the overflow controls host's stack, which then has no clips; the host's stack now gets a copy first.
- `RenderGeometryMap::pushMappingsToAncestor(layer, nullptr)` for a layer more than one level below the root pushed the steps child first, so transforms applied before the offsets inside them; ancestors are pushed first now. The compositor never hits it (it pushes one level at a time).
- `RenderLayerBacking::updateContentsRects` snapped an image's contents clipping rect in the renderer's coordinates and then moved it by the unsnapped offset into the layer, while the contents rect is snapped after the move; an image at a fractional position was clipped a fraction of a pixel inside its contents, fading an edge. The clip is snapped after the move now.
- Krystal.UI and Krystal.Gfx bugs found by compositing are in *G12b as built*.
**Added (upstream API):** listed in the table; `RenderText::HasRenderedText`, `RenderLayerScrollableArea::UsesCompositedScrolling`, `ScrollPositioningBehavior`, `RenderingUpdateStep::LayerFlush`, `RenderBoxModelObject::ContentChangeType`.
**Differences:**
- Without a graphics layer factory pages don't composite and paint as before (the Booey tests; upstream without accelerated compositing).
- The compositor fills the scroll corner layer with the view's background before painting it: Booey's theme draws no corner.
- `PaintScrollbar` is a free function declared in the compositor's header, which the frame view uses too.
Tests: `tests/Rendering/RenderLayerCompositor.cpp` (the root composites with the host's factory, its layer tree, filters and 3D transforms composite where a 2D rotation doesn't, overlap, repaints reaching a backing): 4 cases pass; `tests/Rendering/LayerOverlapMap.cpp`: 3 cases pass. Krystal.UI's `tests/Repaint.cpp` (composited frames against whole repaints, the repaint rects of the view's layer, images at fractional positions) and `tests/View.cpp`. The whole Booey suite passes (2408 cases; 7 expected failures), and so do Krystal.UI's (56 cases) and Krystal.Gfx's (125 cases).

**Bugs fixed:**
- `GraphicsLayerTextureMapper::pauseAnimation` and `removeAnimation` (Krystal.UI's port of it) changed the graphics layer's animations without telling its `TextureMapperLayer` (no `AnimationChange`), so a paused or removed animation kept playing on the layer until the next animation was added.
- G12b left `RenderImage`'s and `repaintForPausedImageAnimationsIfNeeded`'s `contentChanged` calls as FIXMEs, and Krystal.UI's `setContentsToImage` compared images rather than their current frames: a directly composited animated image kept showing its first frame.
**Added (upstream API):** listed in the table.
**Differences:**
- Only `transform` and `opacity` run on layers, as upstream's `GraphicsLayerTextureMapper` accepts: filter and individual transform property (`translate`, `rotate`, `scale`) animations fail to start (`RunningAccelerated::Failed`) and run on the main thread, recompositing without repainting.
- `KeyframeEffect`'s enum `AcceleratedProperties` is `AcceleratedPropertiesState`: the getter `AcceleratedProperties()` has the same name.
- Layer animations sample the event loop's current time (`EventLoop::Current().Now()`) rather than `MonotonicTime::now()`, as the document timeline does, so hosts and tests control it; `TextureMapperAnimation::Resume` takes the time.

The whole Booey suite passes (2411 cases; 7 expected failures), and so do Krystal.UI's (61 cases).

## Composited scrolling (G12d, 2026-10-21)

Part G12d of compositing (*G12 plan* and *G12d plan* in `docs/gfx/DESIGN.md`), in two parts: overflow scrolling layers (G12d1) and fixed layers (G12d2). No new upstream files: G12b ported the scrolling halves of the backing and the compositor behind the switches upstream's drawing area and settings turn on; G12d turns them on, as the coordinated graphics drawing area does, and fills in the paths they guard.

## Plan: freeing documents (decided 2026-10-21)

No document is ever freed (*Open (DOM)* above): every node holds its document (`_nodeDocument` is a `RefPtr`), a document's `_nodeDocument` is itself, and a container never releases its children (the parent's tree reference is released only by removal; a destroyed container would also leave its children's checked parent pointers dangling). So every page a host loads stays in memory, with its render tree's and style's data. The fix mirrors upstream's (`Node`, `TreeScope`, `ContainerNode`, `Document::removedLastRef`); Booey's DOM follows the spec's algorithms rather than upstream's node code, so it's adapted to them. In two parts:

- **M1a, the ownership mechanism** (Krystal.Core, Booey DOM):
  - Krystal.Core's `RefCounted` lets an object whose last reference was dropped stay alive with a reference of its own (upstream's `removedLastRef` for a document whose nodes still reference it); `EventTarget` calls a virtual `RemovedLastRef` that deletes by default.
  - Nodes reference their document without owning it: the document counts its referencing nodes (`incrementReferencingNodeCount`, `decrementReferencingNodeCount`), a document doesn't count itself, and adopting a node moves its count to the new document.
  - A container releases its children when it's destroyed (`removeDetachedChildren`: unlinked without the removal steps, through a deletion queue so deep trees don't recurse).
  - A document whose last reference drops while nodes still reference it clears what retains its nodes (the focused, hovered and active elements, the CSS target, cached collections) and removes its children, then frees itself when the count reaches zero. A document in a frame destroys its render tree when the frame lets it go, before it can be freed.
  - **Tests:** detached subtrees, documents built by hand and parsed ones are freed when the last reference goes (watched through weak pointers); a node adopted into another document keeps that one alive and lets the old one go; nodes held after their document was dropped stay usable.
- **M1b, what retains documents** (Booey, Krystal.UI): with documents freed, the whole suite runs their destructors, which shows what still points at them after they're gone or keeps them alive: render trees, style resolvers and sheets, animation timelines, the event loop's tasks and timers, image and font loaders, mutation observers, node iterators and live collections. Each is fixed as upstream has it (weak or raw back-pointers, clearing on teardown). `View` and `LocalFrame` free the old document when a new page loads. **Tests:** loading pages one after another in a `View` frees the previous documents, with their render trees; the editor page is freed on reload.
- **Out (FIXMEs):** cycles made by the host (event listener callbacks that capture their own target hold it, as they would in a language without garbage collection; noted on `AddEventListener`).
- **As built:** M1b was much smaller than planned: with documents freed, both suites ran clean except for the memory cache singleton being destroyed at exit and one test that read a removed node; render trees, style, animations, loaders and the event loop already let documents go. See *Freeing documents*.

## Freeing documents (M1, 2026-10-21)

*Plan: freeing documents* above, in two parts: the ownership mechanism (M1a) and what retained documents (M1b). Booey's DOM follows the spec's algorithms, so this adapts upstream's mechanism (`Node`, `TreeScope`'s document, `ContainerNode::removeDetachedChildren`, `Document::removedLastRef`) rather than porting files.

| WebKit | Verdict | Krystal | CMake | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `dom/Node.cpp` (the document's referencing-node count in the constructor and destructor, `setTreeScope` on adoption) | `adapted` | `DOM/Node.hpp`, `src/...` | on | tested. `Node::SetNodeDocument` moves the count. |
| `dom/ContainerNode.cpp`, `ContainerNodeAlgorithms.cpp` (`~ContainerNode`, `removeDetachedChildren`, `removeDetachedChildrenInContainer`) | `adapted` | `DOM/ContainerNode.hpp`, `src/...` | on | tested. Children's tree references go through a queue, so deep trees don't recurse. |
| `dom/Document.cpp`, `.h` (`removedLastRef`, `incrementReferencingNodeCount`, `decrementReferencingNodeCount`) | `adapted` | `DOM/Document.hpp`, `src/...` | on | tested. |
| `dom/EventTarget` (`ref`/`deref`, `removedLastRef` for nodes) | `adapted` | `DOM/EventTarget.hpp` | on | `SubRef` calls a virtual `RemovedLastRef`, which deletes by default. |
| `wtf/RefCounted.h` (a count that resumes from zero) | `adapted` | `Krystal.Core/RefCounted.hpp` | on | `ResumeFromNoRefs`, `PrepareToDeleteWithNoRefs`. |
| `loader/cache/MemoryCache.cpp` (`singleton`) | `port` | `Loader/Cache/MemoryCache.hpp`, `src/...` | on | `NeverDestroyed`, as upstream's. |

**Bugs fixed:**
- No document was ever freed: every node held its document, a document's node document was itself, and a container never released its children (its children's parent pointers would also have dangled). Every page a host loaded stayed in memory with its style and render tree data.
- `MemoryCache`'s singleton was destroyed at exit, deleting resources it still listed (`!InCache()` asserted once documents stopped keeping them alive); it's never destroyed now, as upstream's.
- `UserActionElementSet`'s hover test read an element after removing it, which only worked because removed nodes leaked.
**Added (upstream API):** listed in the table.
**Differences:**
- The document keeps its referencing-node count beside Krystal.Core's reference count: when its last reference goes with nodes still referring to it, the count resumes from zero (Krystal.Core's `RefCounted` otherwise forbids references after the last), and the last node to go deletes it.
- Event listener callbacks that hold their own target keep it alive: there's no garbage collector (noted on `AddEventListener`).
Tests: `tests/DOM/NodeLifetime.cpp` (empty, built and parsed documents freed with their trees; detached subtrees freed with their descendants; a node held keeps its document, and both stay usable; adoption moves the reference): 6 cases pass. Krystal.UI's `tests/View.cpp` (a page with layout, composited layers, an animation, a transition and a hovered element is freed when the view loads another page, and when the view goes; the editor page, with its style sheets, fonts and images, is freed and loads again from the memory cache; its animations go with it). The whole Booey suite passes (2419 cases; 7 expected failures), and so do Krystal.UI's (68 cases) and Krystal.Gfx's (129).

- The text iterator doesn't traverse the flat tree, enter text controls or image overlays, or emit text placeholders (FIXMEs; nothing asks for them yet).

**Bugs fixed:** none.
**Added (upstream API):** listed in the table; `LocalFrameView::scheduleSelectionUpdate`, the `selectstart` and `selectionchange` event names, `Node::nonBoundaryShadowTreeRootNode`, the node flag for selection end points.
**Differences:**
- The document owns the selection (`Document::Selection()`), as upstream's documents do; there's one frame per document, and `Document::SetFocusedAndActive` stands in for the focus controller's `setFocused`.
- The theme's platform selection colours are Chrome's: `#3367D1` behind white text when focused and active, `#C8C8C8` behind `#323232` otherwise (upstream's base theme has blue and white, and grey and black). Upstream's blend with white still makes them translucent, which looks the same over white and tints replaced elements.
- The selection's appearance is updated at the rendering update, which `FrameSelection::setSelection` schedules (`LocalFrameView::scheduleSelectionUpdate`); upstream's content relevancy update schedules one there.
- A mouse move carries the held button (Krystal.UI's `View::MouseMoved`), as Windows' moves and upstream's Windows mouse events do, so dragging selects. Moves that don't change the position are dropped there, as Chrome and upstream's Windows port drop them: Windows reports them (raw input reports every press and release as one), and one while the button is held would start a selection.
- `IsSkippedContentRoot(const RenderBox &)` is declared beside `RenderBox` (upstream's is in `RenderBoxInlines.h`); `Determinant`, `SkipExactly` and `AllAtom` moved to shared headers, and `HTMLElement.cpp` and the HTML element files use `infra::StringAlgorithms` directly, for the unity build (2026-10-22; see *Unity build*).
- During a selection, the cursor follows the content beneath it, as Firefox's does: upstream's rule that shows an I-beam over anything while a selection is being dragged is commented out in `EventHandler::SelectCursor` (upstream and Chrome keep it).
- Double clicks don't append trailing whitespace (the editor's `isSelectTrailingWhitespaceEnabled`, off as its client's default is).
Tests: `tests/Editing/VisibleSelection.cpp` (types and order, granularities, trailing whitespace and normalised ranges, editing boundaries): 4 cases; `tests/Editing/FrameSelection.cpp` (setting, selecting all and by the mouse, DOM changes, focus): 4 cases; `tests/Rendering/RenderSelection.cpp` (selection states and gaps, within one text, replaced elements, painting, the theme's colours): 5 cases; `tests/Page/MouseSelection.cpp` (dragging, clicks, what can't be selected): 3 cases. Krystal.UI: the `selection` page golden (Chrome's only reported), and the repaint tests for dragging a selection and autoscrolling. `tests/Page/EventHandler.cpp`'s plain press is now handled, since it places a caret. The whole Booey suite passes (2461 cases; 7 expected failures), and so do Krystal.UI's (74) and Krystal.Gfx's (129).

**Differences:**

**Bugs fixed:** `DeleteSelectionCommand::FixupWhitespace` made a space a two-byte no-break space without moving the positions after it, so the caret landed between its bytes and whitespace rebalancing rewrote the lone `A0` byte (deleting a word before a space left `one\xC2\xA0` corrupted to `one\xC2\xC2\xA0`); the positions after it in the text node now move by the extra byte, and rebalancing snaps offsets to character boundaries and ignores lone continuation bytes. `InputEvent` and `TextEvent` had no type cast traits.
**Added (upstream API):** listed in the table; `Settings::HTMLLegacyAttributeValueSerializationEnabled` and `ShouldConvertPositionStyleOnCopy`; the `beforeinput`, `input`, `textInput`, `beforecut`, `cut`, `beforepaste` and `paste` event names; `Event::IsInputEvent` and `IsTextEvent`; `RenderInline::MayAffectLayout`; `FrameSelection`'s typing style and closing typing on `CloseTyping`; the `style`, `class` and `dir` attribute names.
**Differences:**
- Text offsets are UTF-8 bytes, so the no-break space editing makes is two bytes where upstream's is one UTF-16 unit; whitespace rebalancing steps over it whole, and positions after one that replaces a space move by the extra byte.
- `textInput`'s default action (`Editor::HandleTextEvent`) runs after the event is dispatched, where it isn't cancelled, as Booey's keyboard handlers run theirs; upstream runs it from the node's default event handler.
- `Pasteboard::canSmartReplace` is `CanSmartReplaceContents` (it can't share the name of the `CanSmartReplace` enumerator), and returns false until smart copies are written.
- Pasting into rich content reads the pasteboard's plain text as a fragment (`Pasteboard::ReadDocumentFragment`, as Windows' `documentFragment` does for text); reading web content is a FIXME.
- A paragraph split clones the block, attributes and all (an `id` too), as upstream does.
Tests: `tests/Editing/TypingCommand.cpp` (typing, deleting, line and paragraph breaks, paragraphs in the editable root, input events): 5 cases; `tests/Editing/ApplyStyleCommand.cpp`: 1 case; `tests/Editing/Markup.cpp` (serialising fragments, fragments from markup and text, serialising a selection): 3 cases; `tests/Editing/Editor.cpp` (cutting, pasting): 2 more cases. The editor fixture moved to `Krystal.Booey.Tests/Editing/EditorTestUtils.hpp`. Krystal.UI: `View: the keyboard edits editable text`. The whole Booey suite passes (2486 cases; 7 expected failures), and so do Krystal.UI's (77) and Krystal.Gfx's (129).

**Bugs fixed:**
- `Decimal::ceil` and `floor` tested the scaled-down coefficient for a fractional part, so `ceil` of 1.0 stored as 10e-1 was 2 and `floor(-0.4)` was -0.
- `Event`'s constructor didn't set the initialized flag, so dispatching any event made from a constructor (a `KeyboardEvent` with its init dictionary) threw `InvalidStateError`.
- `FormControlAlgorithms::IsDisabled(option)` and `CollectOptionText` were declared but never defined; `NearestAncestorSelect` walked the ancestors farthest first.
- `HTMLInputElement::DefaultValue` reflected a `defaultvalue` attribute (it's the `value` attribute); `colorSpace` wasn't the enumerated value.
- `EventNames::Cancel` was declared twice; `KeyboardEvent` and `MouseEvent` had no type cast traits for events.

**Added (upstream API):** listed in the table; `ChromeClient::SubmitForm`; `Document::BaseTarget` (the base element's `target`); `Node::TreeScope`; `URLParser::PercentDecode` made public; the `invalid`, `submit`, `reset`, `formdata` and `select` event names; `HTMLProgressElement::MatchesIndeterminatePseudoClass`.
**Differences:**
- `pattern` matches with `std::wregex` (ECMAScript) over UTF-16 rather than Yarr with the `v` flag; an invalid pattern matches anything, as upstream. E-mail addresses match a `std::regex`.
- The form data boundary starts `----BooeyFormBoundary`.
- A type change rebuilds the presentational hints when the type starts or stops respecting `width` and `height`, or being an image button (upstream replays the `width`, `height` and `align` changes for the former).
- `reset()` drops the dirty value directly, as Booey's `SetValue` takes a string view that can't be null (upstream sets a null string).
- The pseudo-class stand-ins in `Style/PseudoClassStateInvalidation.cpp` for form controls are gone, as the controls invalidate their own states; links, `lang`, `dir`, `contenteditable`, `<option>`/`<optgroup>` `disabled` and `<progress>` stay. `InvalidatePseudoClassesForChildChange` went with them.
- `SetValueForUser` doesn't make a value too long or short, as upstream: only typing does (G14c).
Tests: `tests/Platform/Decimal.cpp`: 7 cases; `tests/Platform/DateComponents.cpp`: 3 cases; `tests/HTML/FormListedElement.cpp` (owners, the `form` attribute, labels): 3 cases; `tests/HTML/ValidatedFormListedElement.cpp` (value missing, barred controls, custom validity): 3 cases; `tests/HTML/HTMLInputElement.cpp` (types, sanitising, value modes, validity, numbers and dates, checkboxes, radio groups): 7 cases; `tests/HTML/HTMLFormElement.cpp` (submission and encodings, image buttons, interactive validation, implicit submission, reset): 5 cases. Two invalidation tests changed: a lone option is selected by the selectedness algorithm, and text areas and default buttons invalidate their subtrees, as upstream. Krystal.UI: `View: hands form submissions to the host`. The whole Booey suite passes (2514 cases; 7 expected failures), and so do Krystal.UI's (78; the filters golden differs by a few pixels on battery power).

**Bugs fixed:**
- Booey had dropped revealing the selection after an insertion, so typing past a field's edge didn't scroll it.
- `HTMLTextAreaElement`'s `cols` and `rows` reflected as plain integers: zero, negative and missing values weren't their defaults (20 and 2).

**Added (upstream API):** listed in the table; `Element::DispatchFocusEvent`, `DispatchBlurEvent` and `DidBlur`; `Element::IsTextField`; `Node::IsInUserAgentShadowTree` and `GetRenderBox`; `ElementAlgorithms::AttachUserAgentShadowRoot`; `FocusOptions::SelectionRestoration`; `Event::IsBeforeTextInsertedEvent`; the `webkitBeforeTextInserted`, `focus` and `blur` event names; `infra::NormalizeNewlines`.
**Differences:**
- Selection offsets are UTF-8 byte offsets, as everywhere in Booey's DOM, snapped to character starts; `maxlength` and `minlength` still count UTF-16 units.
- The internal `-webkit-` parts parse only in user agent sheets (upstream lets pages style them).
- No `RenderSearchField`: search fields are `RenderTextControlSingleLine`s without recent searches.
- The spin button waits for the theme (G14d); number fields step with the arrow keys.
- The placeholder sets `-webkit-text-security: none` in code, as Booey's sheet has no prefixed property.
- `ReplaceSelectionCommand` takes a text control's fragment text from the DOM rather than a staging document.
- The resizer grip is drawn as pixels in the theme stand-in rather than from the platform's image.
- Autofill, datalists and the caps lock indicator are FIXMEs.
Tests: `tests/HTML/HTMLTextFormControlElement.cpp` (shadow trees, styling the parts, typing, the selection APIs, passwords, search fields, scrolling to the caret): 7 cases; `tests/Rendering/RenderTextControl.cpp` (the render tree, clicking in a field, dragging a resizer, the settings): 4 cases. `tests/Page/LocalFrameViewScrolling.cpp`'s field got a width, as fields are now their real size. Krystal.UI: `View: typing into text fields`, and the `textfields` golden (report-only against Chrome, whose layout it matches; only the seams between Ahem's glyphs differ). The editor's form card has a required name field and a notes text area. The whole Booey suite passes (2525 cases; 7 expected failures), and so do Krystal.UI's (80).

**Bugs fixed:**
- Setting an option's `text` set an attribute named `text` instead of the option's text.
- An option's `label` was empty without a `label` attribute, instead of its text.
- Options and optgroups didn't invalidate `:disabled` and `:enabled` when their `disabled` attribute changed.
- The list of options didn't skip an optgroup nested in another (a `continue` in the ancestor loop only continued that loop), and the selectedness algorithm picked the first option without its own `disabled` attribute, even in a disabled optgroup.
- Options had renderers; they're drawn by their select.

**Added (upstream API):** listed in the table; `RenderObject::IsRenderMenuList` and `IsRenderListBox`; `RenderTheme::PopupMenuSize`; `RenderBlock::IsPointInOverflowControl` is virtual.
**Differences:**
- Booey parses selects as the current spec does (customizable selects), so the list items are found among all of a select's descendants, as upstream's enhanced select parsing does; the spec's `selectedcontent` cloning is kept from before, still only as the parser pops an option.
- Options keep the spec's dirtiness (upstream's is a FIXME): a dirty option's selectedness doesn't follow its `selected` attribute until a reset.
- An inserted selected option is selected when it's inserted (`OptionInserted`, `OptGroupInserted`), wherever it is in the select, rather than through `childrenChanged`'s change details, which Booey's children-changed hook doesn't have.
- `RenderListBox` is a `ScrollableArea` as upstream, so it has both bases' checked pointer counts; deleting it checks both. It isn't registered with the frame view's scrollable areas, which the view doesn't keep.
- Collections don't cache their items, so `invalidateSelectedItems` does nothing, and `options` and `selectedOptions` make a new collection each time.
- A menu list in a document without a page behaves as with the default chrome client, and has no popup.
- Krystal.UI's popup hides before its client hears the choice, as platform menus do.
Tests: `tests/HTML/HTMLSelectElement.cpp` (list items, selection, options' text and labels, the keyboard and type-ahead): 4 cases; `tests/Rendering/RenderMenuList.cpp` (the selected option's text, the popup through a test chrome client): 2 cases; `tests/Rendering/RenderListBox.cpp` (items, clicks, keys, wheel scrolling, multiple selection): 2 cases. `PseudoClassChangeInvalidation`'s option check reads the computed style, as options have no renderer. Krystal.UI: the popup overlay in `tests/View.cpp`; the `selects` golden (report-only against Chrome) and the `select-popup` golden (no Chrome golden: Chrome's popups are windows). The whole Booey suite passes (2545 cases; 7 expected failures), and so do Krystal.UI's (85).

**Bugs fixed:**
- `LocaleICU::createLabelVector` returned an empty vector rather than null when ICU had no labels, so its callers' fallbacks (English month names, AM and PM) never applied, and the empty labels were then indexed.
- Stepping an empty year field (the arrow keys) set the current year without dispatching `input` and `change`, so the input's value didn't follow it.
- A field's placeholder colour stayed after it got a value: its style wasn't invalidated as its text changed.
- `DeleteSelectionCommand.cpp` used `RenderText` (in a debug assertion) without including it.
- `TextBreakIterator::Locale()` and the generated style getter `Locale()` clashed with the new `Locale` type; they're `GetLocale()` (the property code generator names clashing getters so).

**Added (upstream API):** listed in the table; `LocalTimeNow()` (WTF's local time) in `Platform/DateComponents.hpp`; `ShadowRoot::SetUserAgentDelegatesFocus`; `LocalizedStrings`' `WeekFormatInLDML()`.
**Differences:**
- The user chose (2026-10-23) to focus the fields through Booey's focus model: a date input's user agent shadow root delegates focus, so focusing the input focuses its first field, a click focuses the field under it, and sequential navigation moves between the fields, rather than upstream's input type focus hooks (`handleFocusEvent`, `hasCustomFocusLogic`, `isKeyboardFocusable`). `FocusAlgorithms` treats a user agent shadow root that delegates focus as a focus navigation scope, its parts as click focusable, and the parts of a disabled control as not focusable, and a click on a shadow host that delegates focus focuses its delegate. The fields have `tabindex=0` for upstream's `supportsFocus`.
- The user chose (2026-10-23) to give week inputs fields as Chrome does: a week field and the layout `'Week' ww, yyyy`. Upstream's week inputs have none.
- The fields' placeholder date is a `DateComponents` of today, rather than WTF's `GregorianDateTime`.
- Colour inputs stay focusable by keyboard, as the HTML focus model has them (upstream makes them mouse focusable only).
- Picker choices aren't checked for a user gesture, and `showPicker()` doesn't need transient activation (FIXMEs, as for `<select>`).
- Krystal.UI's pickers hide before telling their client the choice, as its popup does.
- A symbolic field (a month's name, AM or PM) starts its type-ahead again with the key pressed when what was typed matches none of its names (`TypeAhead::ResetSession`, as Chromium's type-ahead has), so `a` then `p` typed quickly switches to PM; upstream searches for `ap` and finds nothing until the keys pause.

Krystal.UI: the date and colour pickers in `tests/View.cpp`; the `dates` golden (report-only against Chrome, which on Windows lays dates out in the system's regional format) and the `date-picker` and `color-picker` goldens (no Chrome goldens: Chrome's pickers are windows). The whole Booey suite passes (2560 cases; 7 expected failures), and so do Krystal.UI's (90).


## Custom elements (B1a, 2026-10-23)

Scoped registries keep Booey's storage (see *Differences*). |

With `CustomElementQueue`, `CustomElementReactionStack`, `CustomElementReactionDisallowedScope` and the backup element queue; `CEReactionsScope` and `CustomElementReactionStackSuspension` are new (see *Differences*). |

| `dom/Element.cpp` (`setIsDefinedCustomElement`, `setIsFailedCustomElement`, `clearReactionQueueFromFailedCustomElement`, `setIsCustomElementUpgradeCandidate`, `enqueueToUpgrade`, `reactionQueue`, `setCustomElementState`), `dom/ElementRareData.h` (the reaction queue) | `port*` | | on | tested. Booey's elements keep the spec's five states; the rare data also holds the element's `CustomElement`. |
| `css/StyleAttributeMutationScope.h` (the custom element half) | `port` | | on | tested. |

**Bugs fixed:**
- The tree builder took an `is` attribute's name for its value.
- `LookupCustomElementDefinition` took no local name, so it couldn't have found a definition (it was unreachable: every path ended in `krys_not_implemented()`).
- `createElement()` without options gave the element a null registry (the default options are a dictionary whose registry is null, which was used as given), so elements made by `createElement()` could never be custom elements. A null registry in the options now leaves the document's, as the spec's *flatten element creation options* does when none is given.
- The parser created elements with an explicit null registry rather than looking one up from the intended parent.
- Nothing set `NodeFlags::IsUnknownElement`, so `Is<HTMLUnknownElement>`, `Is<SVGUnknownElement>` and `Node::IsUnknownElement()` were always false.
- `CustomElementFactory.hpp` forward-declared `Document` in a namespace `boo::dom::dom` (the file is gone: the element factory creates custom elements itself).
- Elements with an `is` value became custom element upgrade candidates (`undefined`, not matching `:defined`); without customized built-ins they're uncustomized, as upstream's.

**Added (upstream API):** listed in the table; `Element::GetCustomElement`, `SetCustomElementRegistry` and `DocumentOrShadowRoot::SetCustomElementRegistry`; `CustomElementAlgorithms::LookUpCustomElementRegistry` (the spec's).
**Differences:**
- The user chose (2026-10-23) behaviour objects for C++ custom elements: an element stays the `HTMLMaybeFormAssociatedCustomElement` it was created as, and its definition's factory creates a `CustomElement` (the host's class) that the element holds, when the element is created synchronously and when it's upgraded, so an element defined after it was created keeps its identity. The callbacks are its virtual methods. A factory that returns null, or a behaviour for another element, is a failure, as a constructor that throws: created synchronously, the element is an `HTMLUnknownElement` in the `failed` state; upgraded, it fails. A synchronously constructed element whose behaviour gave it attributes, children or a parent fails, as upstream's checks.
- The user chose (2026-10-23) no customized built-in elements, as upstream: definitions have no `extends`, and an element's `is` value is kept (cloned and serialised) but doesn't look up a definition.
- The user chose (2026-10-23) to run reactions before the DOM methods the IDL marks `[CEReactions]` return, as upstream's generated bindings do: `CEReactionsScope` (in the members upstream marks `CEReactions=Needed`; built-in elements' members are `NotNeeded`, as they can't be custom) pushes an element queue unless one is on the stack, and `CustomElementReactionStackSuspension` takes the stack away while Booey calls host code (event listeners and the callbacks themselves), so a listener's own calls get their reactions before they return. Editing commands scope their changes (`DoApply`, undo and redo), so their reactions run once the command's changes are made rather than mid-command. Reactions enqueued with no queue on the stack go to the backup element queue. The `[CEReactions]` members Booey doesn't implement yet (`innerHTML`, `outerHTML`, `insertAdjacentHTML`, `setHTMLUnsafe`, `designMode`, `execCommand`, `document.open()` and `write()`, `<dialog>`'s methods, `<table>`'s caption and section members, `popover`, `contentEditable`, `enterKeyHint`, `inputMode`, `nonce`, `DOMStringMap`) get their scope when they're ported.
- Reactions are enqueued for every callback (upstream skips the callbacks a definition lacks; the virtual methods can't be told apart).
- `connectedMoveCallback` (`moveBefore()`), which upstream lacks, is enqueued as the spec has it; by default it calls `DisconnectedCallback` then `ConnectedCallback`, as for a definition without it.
- Registries are stored as Booey's DOM had them, following the spec (each document, shadow root and element holds its registry), rather than upstream's tree scope registries and map of scoped elements.
- A document gets its global registry when it becomes a frame's current document (upstream's comes with the window).
- An upgrade sets the spec's `failed` then `precustomized` states, and `failed` again if it fails (upstream has one `FailedOrPrecustomized` state).
- Failed constructions and upgrades aren't reported (FIXMEs: there's no console).
Tests: `tests/HTML/CustomElement/CustomElementRegistry.cpp` (defining, names, `get`, `getName` and `whenDefined`; creation by the parser, `createElement()` and cloning; upgrades on definition in tree order, on insertion and by `upgrade()`; failures; each callback, observed attributes, the inline style, reaction scopes, the backup queue and a listener's own calls; disabled shadow roots; scoped registries): 7 cases / 131 assertions. The whole Booey suite passes (2567 cases; 7 expected failures), and so do Krystal.UI's (90).

**Bugs fixed:**
- `AbortController::Abort` called `AbortSignal::Abort`, the static `AbortSignal.abort()`, which made a new aborted signal: the controller's own signal was never aborted, so `abort()` did nothing (no abort algorithms, no `abort` event).
- `AbortAlgorithmCallback`'s constructor template took `AbortAlgorithmCallback` itself (it had no move constructor), so moving one, as a signal's list of algorithms does when it grows, wrapped it in a `Func` that moved it again, recursing until the stack overflowed: a signal with two listeners crashed.
- `AbortAlgorithmCallback`'s identity was `std::rand()` (at most 32767), so two algorithms on one signal could compare equal and the second be dropped by `AbortAlgorithms::Add`; identities now come from a counter.

**Added:** `EventTargetAlgorithms::AddEventListener` returns whether it added the listener.
**Differences:**
- The user chose (2026-10-23) handles for listeners added from C++: `AddEventListener(type, Func<void(Event &)>, options)` returns an `EventListenerHandle` (move-only, `[[nodiscard]]`) that removes the listener when it's destroyed, assigned over or `Remove()`d; `Release()` leaves it to the target. `AddEventListener<TEvent>(type, Func<void(TEvent &)>, options)` calls back only for events that are a `TEvent`. The handle holds weak pointers to the target and the registered `EventListener` and removes that listener by identity, so a listener already removed (by `once`, an aborted signal, the target going) is left alone, and an already aborted signal gives an empty handle. It doesn't raise the target's reference count to remove, so a handle that goes with its target's custom element behaviour is safe. Released listeners can be removed together by a shared signal.
- Krystal.UI's `View::DefineCustomElement` (the user's choice, 2026-10-23) keeps a definition and defines it in each document the view loads, before parsing, and in the current document; it stands in for a hook when a document is created until there's navigation (B3).
Tests: `tests/DOM/EventListenerHandle.cpp` (calls, removal by destruction, `Remove()`, assignment and moves, `Release()`, `once`, a signal shared by released listeners, an aborted signal, a dropped target, a listener removing itself during dispatch, typed listeners): 3 cases. Krystal.UI: `tests/View.cpp`, a view's definitions in loaded and current pages, and the editor page's `<bean-rating>` (rated by a click, the arrow keys and a digit, submitted, valid and invalid, reset, and freed with its page). The whole Booey suite passes (2574 cases; 7 expected failures), and so do Krystal.UI's (92).


## Links and the loader (B2a, 2026-10-23)

Part B2a of hyperlinks (*B2 plan* in `docs/booey/ROADMAP.md`): links followed through a slim frame loader that asks the host, the hyperlink utilities, and `USVString` (which held no string, so no URL attribute could be read).

| `loader/FrameLoaderTypes.h` (part) | `port*` | `Loader/FrameLoaderTypes.hpp` | on | `PolicyAction`, `FrameLoadType`, `NewFrameOpenerPolicy`, `NavigationType`, `NavigationHistoryBehavior`. |

| `html/HTMLAreaElement.h`/`.cpp` (the link half) | `port*` | `HTML/HTMLAreaElement.hpp`, `src/...` | on | tested. B2d does the shape half. |

| `dom/UIEventWithKeyState.cpp` (`findEventWithKeyState`) | `port` | `DOM/UIEventWithKeyState.hpp` | on | tested. |
| `html/HTMLImageElement.cpp` (`isServerMap`) | `port` | `HTML/HTMLImageElement.hpp`, `src/...` | on | tested. |

**Bugs fixed:**
- `USVString` was an empty struct, and every `USVString` reflection (`[Reflect]` and `[ReflectURL]`) returned `NotSupportedError`: `src`, `href`, `action`, `cite`, `ping`, `srcset` and the rest couldn't be read or set. It is now a UTF-8 string type of its own; `[ReflectURL]` completes the URL against the node document's base URL, falling back to the attribute as written.
- Several attributes reflected as the wrong kind: `<img srcset>` and `<source srcset>` as URLs; `<iframe src>`, `<iframe longdesc>`, `<embed src>`, `<input src>`, `<object data>`, `<script src>`, `<track src>` and `<video poster>` as plain strings. `<form action>` and `formAction` didn't return the document's URL without an action, and `<base href>` didn't complete against the fallback base URL.
- `HTMLImageElement::CurrentSrc()` always returned the empty string.
- `Draggable()` returned false for `auto`, rather than true for images and links.
- `HTMLAnchorElement` and `HTMLAreaElement` had no `target` (and the anchor no `hreflang` or `type`) member.
- `ImageInputType.cpp` defined a function `Number` in `krys::boo::html`, which hid the `Number` concept from `Numbers.hpp` in a unity batch that put it first; and `Numbers.hpp` didn't include the concept.

**Added (upstream API):** `LocalFrame::Loader()`; `LocalFrame::Create` and `Page::Create` take the frame's loader client; `ResourceRequest`'s HTTP method; `HTMLImageElement::IsServerMap`; `FindEventWithKeyState`.
**Differences:**
- The user chose (2026-10-23) upstream's loader over a chrome client hook. The client answers a policy decision as it's asked (a `PolicyAction`), rather than through a callback. Without document loading (B3), a navigation to another document the client allows does nothing (a FIXME), and so does a new window: the host opens it itself and answers `Ignore`. Form submissions go through the loader synchronously (upstream's navigation scheduler waits for B3), and `ChromeClient::SubmitForm` is gone. Fragment navigations follow `shouldPerformFragmentNavigation`, without the back and forward cache, framesets and the initial empty document. Requests have no referrer, origin or body yet; `download` is passed on unsanitised (no origins).
- `HTMLAreaElement` stays an `HTMLElement`, as the spec has it (upstream derives it from `HTMLAnchorElement`); the two share `URLDecomposition` and `HyperlinkAlgorithms` (the spec's *follow the hyperlink*, the effective target with dangling markup, `rel` keywords, `ismap` coordinates). Following a link is the elements' activation behaviour (Booey's dispatcher runs it for a click); the middle button's `auxclick` and Enter on a focused link are handled in the default event handler, as upstream. Links in editable content are always live (upstream's default; no `editableLinkBehavior` setting). The focus rules are the spec's, in `FocusAlgorithms`, not upstream's overrides.
- `URLDecomposition::Origin` serialises the origin from the URL (`file://` for files, `null` when opaque), as there are no security origins.
- Krystal.UI: `View::SetNavigationHandler` replaces the form submission handler. It's given a `NavigationRequest` (the URL, the target and whether it opens a window, whether it's within the page, the source element, the button, the modifiers, `download`, and a form's method, content type and body) and answers `Allow` or `Ignore`; a view without one allows everything. The editor allows navigations within its page and shows the rest where it showed submissions.
Tests: `tests/HTML/URLDecomposition.cpp` (4 cases), `tests/HTML/HTMLAnchorElement.cpp` (5), `tests/Loader/FrameLoader.cpp` (4), `tests/HTML/Attributes/ReflectURL.cpp` (2); the form tests record submissions through a loader client (`Loader/NavigationTestUtils.hpp`). Krystal.UI: `tests/View.cpp`, a view asking about links. The whole Booey suite passes (2589 cases; 7 expected failures), and so do Krystal.UI's (93).

- `HTMLAnchorElement`'s type traits had no `Node` overload, so `DynamicDowncast<HTMLAnchorElement>` didn't compile from a node.

**Added (upstream API):** `Document::CSSTarget`, `SetCSSTarget`, `FindAnchor`, `HaveStylesheetsLoaded`, `GotoAnchorNeededAfterStylesheetsLoad`, `DidRemoveAllPendingStylesheet`, `EnqueueHashchangeEvent`, `FinishedParsing`; `LocalFrameView::ScrollToFragment`, `ScrollToAnchorFragment`, `MaintainScrollPositionAtAnchor`, `ScheduleScrollToAnchorAndTextFragment`, `ScrollToAnchorAndTextFragmentNowIfNeeded`; `FrameLoader::FinishedParsing`; `Event::IsHashChangeEvent`.
**Differences:**
- Booey has no end of parsing yet (B3's document lifecycle): the tree builder's `StopParsing` calls `Document::FinishedParsing` (outside fragment parsing), which only asks the frame's loader to scroll to the fragment; readiness and the load events are FIXMEs.

- The target is focused through the spec's focusing steps (with the viewport as the fallback, which unfocuses the old element) and becomes the sequential focus navigation starting point; upstream sets the focused element itself.

- The task that scrolls to the anchor keeps the view alive rather than holding a weak pointer (`LocalFrameView` has two weak pointer bases). The maintained anchor is held weakly, so it doesn't keep its document alive.

**Bugs fixed:**
- A collapsed live `Range` in a highlight painted the rest of its text box: `RangeForTextBox` takes equal start and end offsets as a start. Collapsed ranges are skipped whether live or static (upstream only skips static ones).

**Added (upstream API):** `Document::GetHighlightRegistry` (upstream's `highlightRegistry`), `HighlightRegistryIfExists`, `FragmentHighlightRegistry`, `FragmentHighlightRegistryIfExists`, `HasHighlight`, `UpdateHighlightPositions`, `FragmentDirective`; `AbstractRange::IsLiveRange`, `StartBoundaryPoint`, `EndBoundaryPoint`, `MakeSimpleRange(const AbstractRange &)`, `StaticRange`'s type traits; `Settings::ScrollToTextFragmentEnabled` and `ScrollToTextFragmentMarkingEnabled` (both on); `LocalFrameView::ScrollToTextFragment`.
**Differences:**
- The range finder runs the spec's search over each block's text nodes, without upstream's first attempt with `findPlainText` (find in page, with collation, which Booey doesn't have): matching ignores ASCII case only (as upstream's fallback does), and quotation marks fold to their straight forms.
- `Document::SetURL` takes the fragment directive from every URL it's given (empty when there's none), so a link to a text fragment within the page works and a later plain fragment isn't sent to the old text; upstream keeps the first directive (or the page's main frame fragment).
- Revealing the text: `TemporarySelectionChange` reveals the temporary selection itself, as Booey's `FrameSelection::SetSelection` defers revealing to the rendering update (it schedules a layout to update the selection, so a layout is always pending), by which time the temporary selection is gone; `TemporarySelectionChange` is a friend of `FrameSelection` for that. Revealing only forward isn't supported (a FIXME). For the same reason each reveal lays out again, and the layout schedules another reveal, so the pending range is revealed again only once layout has moved it (its ends' caret bounds changed).
- Live ranges in highlights have their positions worked out at every rendering update (upstream only for those that changed, which `Range` doesn't track yet; a FIXME).
- Out (FIXMEs): the text indicator, the text directive generator, revealing `<details>` (B4), the custom highlights' `::spelling-error` and `::grammar-error` types' painting (document markers), the text extraction and app highlights.
Tests: `tests/DOM/FragmentDirectiveParser.cpp` (1 case), `tests/DOM/FragmentDirectiveRangeFinder.cpp` (1: start text, ranges, prefixes and suffixes, word boundaries, quotes, hidden text, several directives), `tests/DOM/Highlight.cpp` (5: the set, the registry, `::highlight()` painting, a live range, `::target-text`), `tests/Loader/FragmentNavigation.cpp` (+1: a text fragment, retries and their timeout). **Differences:**

- `close()` closes any page: it doesn't check that the page is script-closable (one session history entry, which a page always has until B3c) or ask `beforeunload` (B3b): FIXMEs.
- `originAgentCluster` is false (no `Origin-Agent-Cluster`; upstream lacks it).
- Out until later steps: `location`, `history`, `navigation` (B3b, B3c, B3e), the CSSOM View members, `getComputedStyle()` and `getSelection()` (B3a2), timers and frames (B3a3), prompts, `open()` and the global scope's members (B3a4), the navigator (B3a5), storage (B3a6), event handler attributes (B3a7).

## The window's timers and animation frames (B3a3, 2026-10-23)

Step B3a3 of document navigation (*B3 plan* in `docs/booey/ROADMAP.md`): timers, microtasks, animation frame callbacks and idle callbacks, taking C++ functions, and the window's timestamps.

No throttling of timers that change nothing visible, no alignment, no nested-timer map (both power optimisations), no user gesture forwarding. |
| `dom/ScriptedAnimationController.h`/`.cpp` | `port*` | `DOM/ScriptedAnimationController.hpp`, `src/...` | on | tested. No throttling below the page's rate. |
| `dom/IdleCallbackController.h`/`.cpp`, `dom/IdleDeadline.h`/`.cpp` | `port*` | `DOM/IdleCallbackController.hpp`, `DOM/IdleDeadline.hpp`, `src/...` | on | tested. The deadline is given by the idle period, not computed by a window event loop. |

| `page/LocalDOMWindow.cpp` (`setTimeout`, `setInterval`, their clears, `requestAnimationFrame`, `cancelAnimationFrame`, `requestIdleCallback`, `cancelIdleCallback`, `nowTimestamp`, `freezeNowTimestamp`, `unfreezeNowTimestamp`, `frozenNowTimestamp`) | `port*` | | on | tested. Plus `queueMicrotask()`. |
